phrases.translation: That was a community that had already gone before. For them is what they earned and for you is what you have earned. And you will not be accountable for what they have done
phrases.ar: تِلۡكَ أُمَّةٞ قَدۡ خَلَتۡۖ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتۡ وَلَكُم مَّا كَسَبۡتُمۡۖ وَلَا تُسۡـَٔلُونَ عَمَّا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The community meant is explained first, and the exposition of the interpretation of the saying is given.

The word used for one who has passed away is then examined. It is only said of a person who has died and gone, because of his separation from what was his company, and the reason is given at length.

The address that follows is then explained. The Jews and the Christians are told that what belongs to the prophets and messengers of Allah is theirs, and the sense of that is set out.

Those who attribute the doctrines of those communities to themselves are then told that they will not be called to account for what they have fabricated, so the saying is a warning that the deeds of the earlier community do not pass to them.

phrases.translation: The Jews and Christians each say, “Follow our faith to be ˹rightly˺ guided.”
phrases.ar: وَقَالُواْ كُونُواْ هُودًا أَوۡ نَصَٰرَىٰ تَهۡتَدُواْۗ قُلۡ
phrases.explanation:
The claim of the two groups is explained first. By and you will be rightly guided, the sense is that then you will hit upon the path of truth, and another saying in the Quran is cited as a witness for that.

The reply that follows is then introduced, and the wording of it is set out.

The word for religion is then explained. It is the way of faith, so the two are not two separate things in the reply but one thing described in two words.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “No! We follow the faith of Abraham,
phrases.ar: بَلۡ مِلَّةَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ
phrases.explanation:
The case of the word for Abraham's religion is then explained. In these words the noun stands in the accusative, and the reason for that is given.

A second way of accounting for it is then given. The accusative is taken to be caused by a verb that is left unexpressed but understood as we follow.

It is also possible, the reading continues, that it stands in the accusative as an exhortation, that is as an urging toward following the religion of Abraham.

Some of those who recite the Quran read the words in the nominative, and the explanation of that reading is given according to the reciters themselves.

phrases.translation: the upright—who was not a polytheist.”
phrases.ar: حَنِيفٗاۖ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ
phrases.explanation:
The uprightness named in the reply is explained at length. Allah advanced on behalf of His messenger the most eloquent and the most concise of speech, and the wording used is set out, with the reasons given.

The word for uprightness is then examined. It means the straight of everything, and it has been said of the person whose one faith covers every part of him and who does not turn to anything else. The reports naming who said that are given.

The meaning of the statement is then given as a whole, that the reply declares that the religion of Abraham is followed, that it is upright, and that the speaker was not one of those who associated partners with Allah.

And others said that the word means the follower, as was described earlier, and the report naming who said that is given.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O believers,˺ “We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us;
phrases.ar: قُولُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡنَا وَمَآ أُنزِلَ
phrases.explanation:
The address is explained first. The command to say is directed to the believers, and it is to be said to the Jews and the Christians who are being addressed.

The meaning of faith is then given. It is holding for true, so believing here means accepting as true what is named.

The second item of the creed is then explained. What has been sent down to us is the Book that Allah sent down, and the sense is that the believers hold it for true as well.

phrases.translation: and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and his descendants; and what was given to Moses, Jesus, and other prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them. And to Allah we all submit.”
phrases.ar: إِلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَ وَٱلۡأَسۡبَاطِ وَمَآ أُوتِيَ مُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ وَمَآ أُوتِيَ ٱلنَّبِيُّونَ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيۡنَ أَحَدٖ مِّنۡهُمۡ وَنَحۡنُ لَهُۥ مُسۡلِمُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The earlier scriptures are then named in turn. What was sent down to Abraham is the same thing as what was sent down to us, so the believers hold it for true as well.

What was given to Moses and to Jesus is then explained. It is the Torah that Allah gave to Moses and the Gospel that He gave to Jesus, and the believers likewise believe in both, so what the verse lists is a set of books rather than a set of persons.

The closing clause is then explained. By we are submitted to Him, the sense is that the believers submit to Allah, and the explanation of that is given with the rest of the sentence.

phrases.translation: So if they believe in what you believe, then they will indeed be ˹rightly˺ guided.
phrases.ar: فَإِنۡ ءَامَنُواْ بِمِثۡلِ مَآ ءَامَنتُم بِهِۦ فَقَدِ ٱهۡتَدَواْۖ
phrases.explanation:
The condition is explained first. If they believe in the like of that in which you believe, then they have been rightly guided, and the sense given is set out at length.

What the verse establishes is then stated. It shows that Allah accepts no deed from anyone except those who believe in this way, so the condition is the test that decides whose work is taken.

A reading that has been transmitted is then noted. It comes from Ibn Abbas and the copies of the Muslims have taken it, and the reading is given.

The interpretation of that reading is then addressed. It does not rest on the meaning toward which the reading was directed, and what it actually means is set out.

phrases.translation: But if they turn away, they are simply opposed ˹to the truth˺.
phrases.ar: وَّإِن تَوَلَّوۡاْ فَإِنَّمَا هُمۡ فِي
phrases.explanation:
The warning is then explained. And if they turn away, the sense given is that if they turn away from what they have been given, then the consequence of that is stated.

The rest of the clause is then set out, and the account of it explains what is left for those who turn away and what is not.

phrases.translation: But Allah will spare you their evil. For He is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.ar: شِقَاقٖۖ فَسَيَكۡفِيكَهُمُ ٱللَّهُۚ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
phrases.explanation:
The word for division is then explained. Its origin, according to us, comes from the saying of a person who splits something in two, and the account of that is given.

The assurance that closes the verse is then explained. So Allah will suffice you against them, the sense is that the believers need no helper against those who turn away, because Allah deals with them, and the explanation of that is given at length.

phrases.translation: This is the ˹natural˺ Way of Allah. And who is better than Allah in ordaining a way?
phrases.ar: صِبۡغَةَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَنۡ أَحۡسَنُ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ صِبۡغَةٗۖ
phrases.explanation:
The word for coloring is explained first. By it, the meaning is the coloring of Islam, so what the verse refers to is the way of life the believers are in.

The case of the word is then discussed. Whoever reads it in the accusative places it there as a connection to the creed, so it is joined to what it qualifies.

It is also permissible to place it in the nominative, in a manner other than that, namely as the beginning of a new sentence, and the account of that is given.

And it is also permissible to place it in the accusative in a manner other than as a connection to the creed, and the reason for that is explained.

In accordance with what has been said about the meaning of the word, a group of the exegetes have spoken, and the report naming who said that is given.

phrases.translation: And we worship ˹none but˺ Him
phrases.ar: وَنَحۡنُ لَهُۥ عَٰبِدُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The closing words are explained. By and we are worshippers of Him, the sense is that they alone are worshipped, and the rest of the clause is set out.

The sentence is then identified as a command from Allah to His messenger, so what is said in it is what the messenger is to declare, and the account of that is given.

phrases.translation: Say, “Would you dispute with us about Allah, while He is our Lord and your Lord? We are accountable for our deeds and you for yours. And we are devoted to Him ˹alone˺
phrases.ar: قُلۡ أَتُحَآجُّونَنَا فِي ٱللَّهِ وَهُوَ رَبُّنَا وَرَبُّكُمۡ وَلَنَآ أَعۡمَٰلُنَا وَلَكُمۡ أَعۡمَٰلُكُمۡ وَنَحۡنُ لَهُۥ مُخۡلِصُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The question is explained first. Do you dispute with us about Allah, and the sense given is that the address is to say to them, do you contend with us and argue about Him, when He is our Lord and your Lord.

The two claims that follow are then set out. Our deeds are ours and your deeds are yours, and no one is responsible for the deeds of another.

The closing clause is then explained. And we are sincerely devoted to Him alone means that we are devoted to Him alone, with no partner joined to Him.

The whole passage is then placed. It is a rebuke to the Jews and an argument on behalf of the people of faith, and the account of that is given.

phrases.translation: Do you claim that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and his descendants were all Jews or Christians?” Say, “Who is more knowledgeable: you or Allah?” Who does more wrong than those who hide the testimony they received from Allah? And Allah is never unaware of what you do
phrases.ar: أَمۡ تَقُولُونَ إِنَّ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَ وَٱلۡأَسۡبَاطَ كَانُواْ هُودًا أَوۡ نَصَٰرَىٰۗ قُلۡ ءَأَنتُمۡ أَعۡلَمُ أَمِ ٱللَّهُۗ وَمَنۡ أَظۡلَمُ مِمَّن كَتَمَ شَهَٰدَةً عِندَهُۥ مِنَ ٱللَّهِۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The recitation of the opening question is discussed first. There are two possibilities in the recitation, and the first is with the letter that makes it read as you say, so the question is put to those addressed.

The other possibility is given. It is with the letter that makes it read as they say, and whoever recites it that way takes the question to be about what others have said rather than about what the speakers themselves have said.

Some linguists have asserted that when it is recited with the second letter and what follows is a command, the sense is that it is being said to the people addressed that their companions say so.

The reading preferred is then stated. The correct view in our opinion is the first, and the reason is given at length.

The question itself is then explained. It refers to the Jews and the Christians who said to the messenger and his companions that they should be Jews or Nazarenes for the way to be followed.

Others said that what is meant is the question about the one who conceals a testimony, and the report naming who said that is given.

The view already stated is then preferred, and the reason is given, since what the verse says points to it.

phrases.translation: That was a community that had already gone before. For them is what they earned and for you is what you have earned. And you will not be accountable for what they have done
phrases.ar: تِلۡكَ أُمَّةٞ قَدۡ خَلَتۡۖ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتۡ وَلَكُم مَّا كَسَبۡتُمۡۖ وَلَا تُسۡـَٔلُونَ عَمَّا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The sense of the verse is given at length. It is said to the messenger to those who dispute with him about Allah among the Jews and the Christians: if they conceal the testimony they hold about Abraham and about the fact that they were Muslims, while claiming that they were Jews or Christians and so lying, then truly Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the patriarchs were a community that has passed away, meaning that it has gone its way and returned to its Lord.

What belongs to that community is then set out. It has with Allah what it earned of good and what it earned of evil, and nothing benefits it except its good deeds and nothing harms it except its bad deeds.

The consequence for those addressed is then drawn, since they are the ones in whom they take pride. They are told to hasten to repentance before departing from this life and to abandon reliance on the merits of the fathers.

phrases.translation: The foolish among the people will ask, “Why did they turn away from the direction of prayer they used to face?”
phrases.ar: سَيَقُولُ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَا وَلَّىٰهُمۡ عَن قِبۡلَتِهِمُ ٱلَّتِي كَانُواْ عَلَيۡهَاۚ قُل
phrases.explanation:
The claim of the ignorant is explained first. The foolish will say, and the sense given is that the ignorant ones will ask about what they consider a matter, and the wording of the question is set out.

It has been said that the foolish are the hypocrites, and the report naming who said that is given.

The reason for the word used is then explained. Allah called them foolish only because they held the truth to be folly, so the word describes their judgement of the matter rather than their understanding of it.

The question itself is then explained. What has turned them away from their prayer direction, and the sense given is what thing has turned away and diverted the faces of these people from the place they used to face.

The word for prayer direction is then examined. The prayer direction of each thing is that which its face faces toward, and the form of the word and its derivation from the saying of a person who comes to stand opposite someone are given at length.

The whole sentence is then set out. The question is put to the believers when they turn their faces away from the prayer direction of the Jews, which was a prayer direction for them before the command to turn toward the sacred mosque.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “The east and west belong ˹only˺ to Allah. He guides whoever He wills to the Straight Path.”
phrases.ar: لِّلَّهِ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقُ وَٱلۡمَغۡرِبُۚ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٖ مُّسۡتَقِيمٖ
phrases.explanation:
The reply is explained first. To Allah belongs the east and the west, and the sense is that the dominion covers what lies between the two extremities of the place of sunrise and the two extremities of its place of sunset, and what is between them of the world.

The guidance named in it is then explained. He guides whom He wills of His creatures, meaning that He aids him onto the right way and leads him successfully to the straight path, and the straight path is the prayer direction of Abraham, whom He made a leader for the people. And He forsakes whom He wills of them, and leads him astray from the way of the truth.

The occasion of the question is then given. The messenger prayed in the direction of Jerusalem for a period, and the account of how long that period lasted is given, with the reports naming who said what recorded with it. Some said it came by the choice of the messenger himself, and others said it was on the basis of a prior instruction.

The occasion for the question is then stated in turn. It arose when the people who asked why they had been turned away saw the change of direction, and the reason for the prayer in that direction in the first place is given.

The wording of the reply is then explained. Say to Allah belongs the east and the west, He guides whom He wills to a straight path, and the sense given is that the messenger is to say this to those who said to him and his companions what has turned you away from your prayer direction of Jerusalem toward the sacred mosque.

phrases.translation: And so We have made you ˹believers˺ an upright community so that you may be witnesses over humanity and that the Messenger may be a witness over you.
phrases.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ أُمَّةٗ وَسَطٗا لِّتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ شَهِيدٗاۗ
phrases.explanation:
The phrase made upright community is explained first. The sense is that just as the believers have been guided by means of the messenger and what he brought them from Allah, and just as they have been given the favour of success in following the prayer direction of Abraham and his creed, so too they have been singled out and favoured above the adherents of other religions in being made an upright community.

The word for community was explained earlier, meaning the generation of people and the grouping among them. The word for upright is then examined. In the language of the Arabs it means the best and the choicest, and a person is said to be the choicest of his lineage when the loftiness of his lineage is meant.

The meaning of upright is also given as just and equitable, since the choicest among people are their just ones, and the reports naming those who said that are given.

The witnessing named next is then explained. The sense is that the community has been made upright and just so that it may be witnesses for the prophets and messengers concerning their communities, regarding the conveyance of the message, and so that the messenger may be a witness over the believers concerning their belief in him.

phrases.translation: We assigned your former direction of prayer only to distinguish those who would remain faithful to the Messenger from those who would lose faith.
phrases.ar: وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡقِبۡلَةَ ٱلَّتِي كُنتَ عَلَيۡهَآ إِلَّا لِنَعۡلَمَ مَن يَتَّبِعُ ٱلرَّسُولَ مِمَّن يَنقَلِبُ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيۡهِۚ
phrases.explanation:
The reason the former prayer direction was appointed is then explained. The sense is that the appointment of that direction, and the turning away from it toward the sacred house, was to distinguish the one who follows the messenger from the one who turns back on his heels, and the direction meant is the one they used to face before the turn toward the house.

A point of grammar is then added. The mention of the turning away from it was omitted because the indication of the earlier part of the statement toward the intended meaning was enough, as in the other comparable cases already mentioned.

phrases.translation: It was certainly a difficult test except for those ˹rightly˺ guided by Allah.
phrases.ar: وَإِن كَانَتۡ لَكَبِيرَةً إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَى ٱللَّهُۗ
phrases.explanation:
The reasoning behind the testing is then given at length. The trial that the companions of the messenger underwent over the prayer direction came when the direction changed from Jerusalem to the house, until some who had converted apostatised and many hypocrites revealed themselves. So it was a trial for the people and a purification for the believers.

A question of wording is then addressed. He ascribed the asking and the visiting to Himself, while in reality it concerned someone else. And by that We might distinguish, the sense is that His protected ones might distinguish.

This is then set aside as far-fetched. Seeing does stand in place of knowing, so it is sound to indicate knowledge by the mention of seeing, but it is not sound to indicate seeing by the mention of knowing, which is not found in the language of the Arabs.

Others said that the phrase means only that His protected ones might distinguish, while He knew before it came to pass, out of gentleness toward His servants.

The two sides of the testing are then explained. The one who follows the messenger follows him in what Allah commands, and the one who turns back on his heels is the one who apostatises or opposes the messenger.

What was grave is then discussed. Some said the word means the turning away from Jerusalem toward the sacred house. Others said it means the prayer direction itself, and others that it means the prayer they performed there.

The interpretation preferred is then given. It is the turning of the face of the messenger from the first direction toward the other that fell grave upon them, and not the direction itself nor the prayer.

The exception is then explained. The change was weighty, except for the one to whom Allah granted success.

phrases.translation: And Allah would never discount your ˹previous acts of˺ faith.
phrases.ar: وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَٰنَكُمۡۚ
phrases.explanation:
The word faith is explained first. It has been said that in this place the prayer is meant.

The sense of faith was expounded earlier. It is the holding-true, and that may come by the statement alone or by the deed alone or by both together, so what is meant is that Allah would not let the holding-true of his messenger, which the believers showed by praying as they were commanded toward Jerusalem, be lost.

An objection is then answered. The people addressed were anxious about their brothers who had died while praying toward Jerusalem, so how can Allah say of the living that he would not let their faith be lost. They were anxious about the reward of that prayer too, supposing it had become null. The verse was therefore addressed to the living with the dead among them included.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is Ever Gracious and Most Merciful to humanity
phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِٱلنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفٞ رَّحِيمٞ
phrases.explanation:
The closing words are then explained. Allah is toward mankind full of compassion and merciful, and the sense is that Allah is toward all His servants the possessor of compassion, and compassion is the highest of the meanings of mercy and is general for all creatures in this world and for some of them in the hereafter, while the Merciful is the possessor of mercy for the believers.

The recitation of the word for compassion is then discussed. It is the reading of most of the reciters of Kufa in one form, and the reading of most of the reciters of Medina in another, and the accepted reading is one of the first two.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We see you ˹O Prophet˺ turning your face towards heaven. Now We will make you turn towards a direction ˹of prayer˺ that will please you.
phrases.ar: قَدۡ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجۡهِكَ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِۖ فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبۡلَةٗ تَرۡضَىٰهَاۚ فَوَلِّ وَجۡهَكَ شَطۡرَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۚ
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. By We see the turning of your face toward the heaven, the sense given is that We see how you turn and direct yourself.

The word for turning is then explained. It means the turning about and the directing. And by toward the heaven, the meaning is in the direction of the heaven and toward its side, so the verse pictures the messenger looking up and waiting.

Why he longed for it is then discussed. Others said that he longed for it because it was the prayer direction of his father Abraham, and the report naming who said that is given.

The promise that follows is then explained. By We will surely turn you to a prayer direction that pleases you, the sense is that We will turn you to a direction that pleases you, and by so turn your face, the sense is that you should turn your face and change its direction.

phrases.translation: So turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque ˹in Mecca˺—wherever you are, turn your faces towards it.
phrases.ar: وَحَيۡثُ مَا كُنتُمۡ فَوَلُّواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ شَطۡرَهُۥۗ
phrases.explanation:
The command about turning the face is explained first. By wherever you may be, turn your faces toward it, the sense given is that wherever the believers may be on the earth, they are to turn their faces toward the sacred mosque, and the suffix in its direction refers to the sacred mosque.

A disagreement about the door is then recorded. Others said that the entire house is a prayer direction, and that the prayer direction of the house is its door, and the report naming who said that is given.

The ruling preferred is then given at length. It is what Allah said, that you should turn your face in the direction of the sacred mosque, and whoever turns his face in that direction is the one who has correctly faced the prayer direction. It suffices for the one who directs himself toward it that he have the intention in his heart that he is directing himself toward it, just as the one who follows an imam is only obliged to follow him even if his body is not directly in line with the imam, and even if he stands at one end of the row while the imam is at the other end, provided he is behind him and praying in the direction in which the imam prays. So too is the ruling of the prayer direction, for when he is to the right or to the left of it and facing it, he directs himself toward it validly, whether the distance be great or small, provided he does not turn his back to it.

The saying of the messenger is then given, that the house is the prayer direction and the prayer direction of the house is its door.

phrases.translation: Those who were given the Scripture certainly know this to be the truth from their Lord.
phrases.ar: وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ لَيَعۡلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡۗ
phrases.explanation:
The second half of the verse is explained first. By those who were given the Book, the sense is that the scribes of the Jews and the scholars of the Christians.

The knowledge named is then set out. By know for certain that it is the truth from their Lord, the sense is that these rabbis and scholars know for certain that the change of the prayer direction is the truth from their Lord, and by from their Lord, the meaning is that it is a binding obligation upon the servants of Allah and not a matter of their choice.

phrases.translation: And Allah is never unaware of what they do
phrases.ar: وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا يَعۡمَلُونَ
phrases.explanation: The closing words are then explained. By Allah is not unaware of what you do, the sense given is that Allah is not unaware of what the believers do, so the statement warns them that their deeds are watched, and the account of that is given.

phrases.translation: Even if you were to bring every proof to the People of the Book, they would not accept your direction ˹of prayer˺, nor would you accept theirs; nor would any of them accept the direction ˹of prayer˺ of another.
phrases.ar: وَلَئِنۡ أَتَيۡتَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِكُلِّ ءَايَةٖ مَّا تَبِعُواْ قِبۡلَتَكَۚ وَمَآ أَنتَ بِتَابِعٖ قِبۡلَتَهُمۡۚ وَمَا بَعۡضُهُم بِتَابِعٖ قِبۡلَةَ بَعۡضٖۚ
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. By even if you were to come to those who were given the Book with every proof and every argument, the sense given is that even if the messenger came with every proof that the truth is what he has brought them, namely the change of the prayer direction to the sacred mosque, they would still refuse to hold that to be true and would not follow the prayer direction toward which he has been turned.

A point of grammar is then given at length. The words for even if are answered with the past tense of the verb, whereas by rule they would be answered with the future tense, in assimilation to the words for if. The reason is that the conditional clause resembles an oath, since it is not valid except by what confirms it afterward.

The clause about not being followers of one another's prayer direction is then explained. The sense is that the Jews and the Christians do not agree upon a single prayer direction, since if he follows the prayer direction of the Jews he embitters the Christians, and if he follows that of the Christians he embitters the Jews.

He is then told to leave off what cannot be satisfied and to call them to the pure creed and the prayer direction of Abraham and the prophets after him.

phrases.translation: And if you were to follow their desires after ˹all˺ the knowledge that has come to you, then you would certainly be one of the wrongdoers
phrases.ar: وَلَئِنِ ٱتَّبَعۡتَ أَهۡوَآءَهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَكَ مِنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ إِنَّكَ إِذٗا لَّمِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. By even if you were to follow their desires, the sense given is that even if the messenger sought the satisfaction of these Jews and Christians, who said to him and his companions, be Jews or Christians, then you will be rightly guided, and were then to follow their prayer direction, that is to say, were then to return to it.

The clause that follows is then explained. By after the knowledge has come to you, the meaning is after the knowledge has reached the messenger, in that it has been made known to him that they persist in falsehood and in obstinate resistance against the truth, and that they know the prayer direction toward which he has been turned is the very one imposed upon Abraham and upon all his descendants among the messengers.

Then you would surely be among the wrongdoers is then explained. The sense is that the messenger, if he were to do that, would be among the servants who wrong themselves, who oppose the command and abandon obedience to Allah.

phrases.translation: Those We have given the Scripture recognize this ˹Prophet˺ as they recognize their own children.
phrases.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ يَعۡرِفُونَهُۥ كَمَا يَعۡرِفُونَ أَبۡنَآءَهُمۡۖ
phrases.explanation: The opening is explained first. By those to whom We have given the Book recognize it, the sense given is that the scribes of the Jews and the scholars of the Christians know that the sacred house is their prayer direction, and the prayer direction of Abraham, and the prayer direction of the prophets before the messenger, just as they recognize their own sons.

phrases.translation: Yet a group of them hides the truth knowingly
phrases.ar: وَإِنَّ فَرِيقٗا مِّنۡهُمۡ لَيَكۡتُمُونَ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُونَ
phrases.explanation: The second half is then explained. By a group of them conceal the truth while believing in it, the sense is that a group of those to whom the Book was given, and they are the Jews and the Christians, conceal the truth even while they believe in it. It has been said that the phrase means the people of the book, and the report of that is given.

phrases.translation: ˹This is˺ the truth from your Lord, so do not ever be one of those who doubt
phrases.ar: ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَ فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡمُمۡتَرِينَ
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. By the truth from your Lord, the sense given is that the messenger should know that the truth is that which his Lord has made known to him and brought to him from Himself, and not that which the Jews and the Christians say to him.

The warning is then explained. By so be not one of those who doubt, the sense is that the messenger should not be one of those who are in doubt about the fact that the prayer direction toward which he has been turned is the prayer direction of Abraham and of the rest of the prophets.

The word used is then examined. It is a derived form from the word for doubt, and a line of poetry is cited as a witness for that sense.

A question is then raised. Was the messenger in doubt about the fact that the truth was from his Lord, such that doubting about it was forbidden to him?

The question is then answered. That belongs to the manner of speech which the Arabs express in the form of a command or a prohibition to the one addressed while another is meant by it, and the example given is the command addressed to the messenger in the verse that begins with the appeal to the prophet to be mindful of Allah and not to obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites.

phrases.translation: Everyone turns to their own direction ˹of prayer˺.
phrases.ar: وَلِكُلّٖ وِجۡهَةٌ هُوَ مُوَلِّيهَاۖ
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. By for everyone, the sense is for every adherent of a religious community, and the rest of the phrase is left out since the wording itself points to it.

The explanation of that view is then given. For every adherent of a religious community there is a prayer direction toward which he turns and toward which he directs his face.

Another view is then set out. For every cardinal direction toward which your Lord has turned you, there is a prayer direction, and Allah turns His servants toward it.

The word for direction is then examined. It is a verbal noun, like the manner of sitting and the manner of walking, derived from turning oneself, and its meaning is that toward which one turns and toward which one directs his face in prayer.

The turning named in it is then explained. It means turning toward, and the Arabic usage is set out, since one says to another, turn to me, in the meaning of turning yourself toward me, and one says I turned toward him when one turns oneself toward him while turning away from something else.

The recitation of the phrase is then discussed. It has been transmitted from Ibn Abbas and others that they read it as he is turned thereto, in the meaning that he is turned toward that direction, and in that case the word everyone has no agent named.

Another reading is mentioned. It has been said that some of them read it as and for every direction, with the omission of the nunation and with the construct annexation, but that is a linguistic error and it is not permissible to read it thus, since the statement would then be incomplete and without meaning, and that is not admissible as coming from Allah.

The reading preferred is then given. It is and for everyone there is a direction toward which he turns, meaning that everyone has a direction and a prayer direction and each of them turns his face toward it, and the reason is the agreement of the reciters of the Quran on that reading and the anomaly of anyone who departs from it.

phrases.translation: So compete with one another in doing good. Wherever you are, Allah will bring you all together ˹for judgment˺. Surely Allah is Most Capable of everything
phrases.ar: فَٱسۡتَبِقُواْ ٱلۡخَيۡرَٰتِۚ أَيۡنَ مَا تَكُونُواْ يَأۡتِ بِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ جَمِيعًاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ قَدِيرٞ
phrases.explanation:
The command to compete is explained first. By so compete in good deeds, the sense given is that the believers should hasten to good works in gratitude toward their Lord and should provide for themselves in this life for the hereafter, since the ways of salvation have been made clear to them. They are told to guard their prayer direction and not to squander it as the peoples before them squandered theirs.

The gathering named next is then explained. By wherever you may be, Allah will bring you all together, the sense is that in whatever place they perish, Allah will bring them all together on the day of resurrection.

The urging of the verse is then set out. It urges the believers to obedience and to providing for themselves, since they are told to compete in works of obedience and to hold fast to the prayer direction of Abraham and to the legal ordinances of his religion, for Allah will bring them and those who opposed them before each other on the day of resurrection, until the doer of good is given his reward and the doer of evil his punishment, or Allah forgives.

The closing words are then explained. By Allah is over all things Almighty, the sense is that Allah is able to gather them after their death from wherever they were, so they should hasten with good works before they die.

phrases.translation: Wherever you are ˹O Prophet˺, turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque. This is certainly the truth from your Lord. And Allah is never unaware of what you ˹all˺ do
phrases.ar: وَمِنۡ حَيۡثُ خَرَجۡتَ فَوَلِّ وَجۡهَكَ شَطۡرَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۖ وَإِنَّهُۥ لَلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكَۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. By from wherever you set out, the sense given is that from whatever place the messenger sets out, and toward whatever place he directs himself, he is to turn his face toward the sacred mosque, and the turning in that direction means directing the face toward it, and the meaning of the word for direction was explained earlier.

The truth named in it is then explained. By and indeed it is the truth from your Lord, the sense is that directing oneself in that direction is the truth concerning which there is no doubt, coming from the Lord, so the messenger is to hold to that and obey Allah in turning toward it.

The closing words are then explained. By Allah is not unaware of what you do, the sense is that Allah is not unaware of the deeds of the believers, and the account of that is given.

phrases.translation: Wherever you are ˹O Prophet˺, turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque. And wherever you ˹believers˺ are, face towards it,
phrases.ar: وَمِنۡ حَيۡثُ خَرَجۡتَ فَوَلِّ وَجۡهَكَ شَطۡرَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۚ وَحَيۡثُ مَا كُنتُمۡ فَوَلُّواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ شَطۡرَهُۥ
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. By from wherever you set out, turn your face toward the sacred mosque, the sense given is that from whatever place or region the messenger departs and sets out, he is to turn his face toward the sacred mosque, for that is its direction.

The command to the believers is then explained. By wherever you are, turn your faces toward it, the sense is that wherever the believers may be, on whatever part of the earth of Allah, they are to turn their faces in their prayer toward it and take it as their goal.

phrases.translation: so that people will have no argument against you, except the wrongdoers among them. Do not fear them; fear Me,
phrases.ar: لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَيۡكُمۡ حُجَّةٌ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مِنۡهُمۡ
phrases.explanation:
The reason given is explained first. By so that the people may have no argument against you, except those among them who do wrong, a group of the exegetes said that the people meant are the people of the book.

That answer is then given. It was said that the people of the book argued that the messenger and his companions did not know where their prayer direction was until they were guided, and that the messenger differs from them in religion yet follows their prayer direction, and that was the argument with which they argued against the messenger and his companions, by way of disputing and as a deception toward the ignorant among the polytheists.

The sense of the disputing is then set out. It concerns only the disputations and the wrangling, and Allah cut off that argument of theirs by turning the prayer direction of the messenger and the believers away from the direction of the Jews toward the direction of Abraham, and that is what is meant by the people having no argument against them, namely those who argued in that manner.

The exception is then explained. Those who do wrong are the polytheists of Quraysh, and the sense of it is set out. The word for argument means precisely the disputation and the wrangling, so the meaning is that none of the people may have a disputation or a false claim against them, except the polytheists of Quraysh, for they have a false claim and a disputation without right in saying that the messenger has returned to their prayer direction and will return to their religion. That is why they alone were excepted.

phrases.translation: so that I may ˹continue to˺ perfect My favour upon you and so you may be ˹rightly˺ guided
phrases.ar: فَلَا تَخۡشَوۡهُمۡ وَٱخۡشَوۡنِي وَلِأُتِمَّ نِعۡمَتِي عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَهۡتَدُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The sense of the exception is then explained at length. It is an exception in the well-known sense, which affirms for the excepted what was denied of the rest, as when one says that no one of the people travelled except your brother. So none of the people has a disputation or a false claim against the messenger or his companions because of their turning toward the house, except those among Quraysh who have wronged themselves, since they have a disputation and a false claim in saying that the believers turned toward them only because they were better guided, and that the turning toward Jerusalem was error.

The claim that the exception means and not is then set aside as false. If that were its meaning, the mention of the exception would add nothing but confusion. And it falls outside the language of the Arabs, since the word for except does not occur with the sense of and except after a preceding exception, as in the saying that the people travelled except Amr and except your brother.

A further claim is then set aside, that the wrongdoers have no argument so should not be feared, and that is rejected on the agreement of all the exegetes in declaring it false.

Another claim is then set aside, that the wrongdoers here are Arabs who were Jews and Christians, and that the argument of whoever argued was broken. That is rejected too, since the exception was directed at wrongdoers among the people of the book, who have a shaky argument against them.

The closing clause is then explained. By so that I may complete My favor upon you, the sense is that by turning the face toward the sacred mosque and taking it as a prayer direction, none of the people may have an argument except the polytheists of Quraysh, and so that by guiding them to the prayer direction of Abraham, whom He made a leader for the people, Allah may complete His favor and perfect His grace upon them and complete the ordinances of the pure community which He charged Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus and the rest of the prophets besides them.

phrases.translation: Since We have sent you a messenger from among yourselves—reciting to you Our revelations, purifying you, teaching you the Book and wisdom, and teaching you what you never knew—
phrases.ar: كَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا فِيكُمۡ رَسُولٗا مِّنكُمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا وَيُزَكِّيكُمۡ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَيُعَلِّمُكُم مَّا لَمۡ تَكُونُواْ تَعۡلَمُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The connection of the words is explained first. The phrase just as is joined to the saying and so that I might complete My favor upon you, and not joined to the saying Remember Me, and I will remember you.

That reading is then defended. The Arabs do not put a condition on the second part of such a phrase, so the clearest proof is that the reply Remember Me follows and the two clauses stand apart.

That view is then rejected as too far-fetched and as driving the saying away from its well-known meaning, and it is not among the most eloquent of the speech of the Arabs.

The sense of just as is then explained. It means the Arabs, so the address is to them to hold fast to obedience and to turn toward the prayer direction they have been commanded to turn toward, so that the argument of the Jews falls away, just as the favor was first bestowed by sending among them a messenger.

The work of the messenger is then set out. By who recites to you Our signs, it means the signs of the Quran. By and purifies you, it means cleanses you of the filth of sins. And teaches you the Book means the Criterion. The wisdom means the transmitted practices and the understanding of religion.

The last clause is then explained. By teaches you what you did not know, it means the reports of the prophets, the accounts of the bygone communities, and the report of what comes to pass among the Arabs which they did not know and learned from the messenger.

phrases.translation: remember Me; I will remember you.
phrases.ar: فَٱذۡكُرُونِيٓ أَذۡكُرۡكُمۡ
phrases.explanation:
The exchange is explained first. By Remember Me, I will remember you, the sense given is that the believers are to remember Allah by obeying Him in what He commands and forbids, and He will remember them through His mercy toward them and His forgiveness for them.

A point of grammar is then added, that the word may be derived from the word for remembrance in the sense of praise and laudation.

phrases.translation: And thank Me, and never be ungrateful
phrases.ar: وَٱشۡكُرُواْ لِي وَلَا تَكۡفُرُونِ
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. By be grateful to Me, the sense given is that the believers are to be grateful to Allah for the favor He has bestowed upon them in the form of Islam and the guidance to the religion He has prescribed for His prophets.

The second half is then explained. By never be ungrateful, the sense is that they are not to deny His beneficence toward them, lest He deprive them of the favor He has bestowed, and rather they are to be grateful so that He may increase them and complete His favor and guide them to that to which He has guided those of His servants with whom He is pleased.

The two words are then explained from what was shown earlier. Gratitude is the praising of a person for his praiseworthy deeds, and ungratefulness is the covering up of a matter.

phrases.translation: O believers! Seek comfort in patience and prayer. Allah is truly with those who are patient
phrases.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱسۡتَعِينُواْ بِٱلصَّبۡرِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. By seek help through patience and prayer, the sense is that the believers are to seek help from what they are commanded to endure and to hold fast to, and the meaning of patience and of prayer was expounded earlier, so it is not repeated.

The closing clause is then explained. By Allah is with the patient, the sense given is that Allah is their helper and their support and is pleased with their deed, and it is like the saying of a man, do such-and-such, and I am with you, meaning that he is their helper in that deed and their support in it.

phrases.translation: Never say that those martyred in the cause of Allah are dead—in fact, they are alive! But you do not perceive it
phrases.ar: وَلَا تَقُولُواْ لِمَن يُقۡتَلُ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَمۡوَٰتُۢۚ بَلۡ أَحۡيَآءٞ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تَشۡعُرُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. By seek help through patience, the sense given is that the believers are to seek help through patience in obeying Allah in the struggle against the enemy, in refraining from disobeying Him, and in fulfilling His obligations.

The prohibition is then explained. Do not say of those killed in the way of Allah that they are dead, since the dead one is the one from whom He has taken his life, and whoever is killed in that way is living with Allah, rejoicing over the favor he has been granted.

An objection is then answered. If the favour of distinguishing the martyrs is not present in this verse, the answer is that they had come to know their state through the earlier report, and since the purpose here was to forbid calling them dead, the repetition was omitted.

The clause about not perceiving them is then explained. By but you perceive it not, the meaning is that they do not see them, so they would know they are living only through the report given to them.

A point of grammar is then added. The word dead is in the nominative because of an implied pronoun referring to those who are killed in the way of Allah, and the same holds of nay, they are living.

phrases.translation: We will certainly test you with a touch of fear and famine and loss of property, life, and crops. Give good news to those who patiently endure—
phrases.ar: وَلَنَبۡلُوَنَّكُم بِشَيۡءٖ مِّنَ ٱلۡخَوۡفِ وَٱلۡجُوعِ وَنَقۡصٖ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَمۡوَٰلِ وَٱلۡأَنفُسِ وَٱلثَّمَرَٰتِۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. It is an announcement from Allah to the followers of His messenger that He will test them and put them to the trial with severe trials in all sorts of matters, so that He may know who follows the messenger and who turns back on his heels, just as He tested them with the change of the prayer direction, and this was promised them in another verse, where they were told that they did not think they would enter the garden before they were given the like of those before them.

The word for trial is then explained. And We will surely test you means that He will surely put them to the trial, and the sense of that word was expounded earlier.

The kinds of trial are then set out. With something of fear means the fear of the enemy. Hunger means famine, so a year of drought befalls them in which hunger and privation come upon them and the obtaining of the necessities of life is made difficult. And wars take place between them and the unbelievers. And the death of their offspring. And droughts occur. All of this is a trial, so that the truthful may be distinguished from the liars and the people of insight from the hypocrites.

A point of grammar is then given. The word for something was used rather than the word for things because of the diversity of the kinds, and since the word for of indicates that with each kind the word for something is understood, the mention of it was enough.

phrases.translation: who, when faced with a disaster, say, “Surely to Allah we belong and to Him we will ˹all˺ return.”
phrases.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَصَٰبَتۡهُم مُّصِيبَةٞ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّآ إِلَيۡهِ رَٰجِعُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. By give glad tidings to the patient ones, the sense given is that the glad tidings are given to those who know that every grace befalling them comes from Him, who therefore acknowledge His claim as Lord over them.

Their state is then described. They submit to His decree, hope for His reward and fear His punishment, and say when He tests them with some of His trials and afflicts them with what He has promised, that they are the possession of their Lord as long as they remain alive and that they will return to Him after death, in submission to His decree and contentment with His judgments.

phrases.translation: They are the ones who will receive Allah’s blessings and mercy.
phrases.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ صَلَوَٰتٞ مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡ
phrases.explanation:
The ones described are explained first. By those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy, the sense is that blessings are sent upon them and mercy is granted to them.

The word for blessing is then explained from what was shown earlier, and it means forgiveness, so what is promised for them is forgiveness.

phrases.translation: And it is they who are ˹rightly˺ guided
phrases.ar: وَرَحۡمَةٞۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُهۡتَدُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The second half is then explained. By those are the ones who are rightly guided, the sense is that they are the ones who have hit upon the path of truth, and the meaning of being rightly guided was explained earlier as correct guidance toward what is right.

It is announced alongside what was said about granting them forgiveness and mercy on account of their steadfast patience under the trials and their submission to His decree, and the report naming who said so is given.

phrases.translation: Indeed, ˹the hills of˺ Ṣafa and Marwah are among the symbols of Allah.
phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلصَّفَا وَٱلۡمَرۡوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ
phrases.explanation:
The names are then examined. As for Marwah, it is the small pebble, and a small quantity of them is gathered together as marawāt and a large quantity as al-marw, and two lines of poetry are cited as a witness.

The word for symbols is then explained. By among the sacred symbols of Allah, the meaning is among the landmarks of Allah which He has made for His servants a marker and a sign by which they worship Him.

The two mountains are then specified. What is meant is the two mountains designated by these two names and located within the sacred precinct, and not the rest of the level ground and the pebbles.

phrases.translation: So whoever performs the pilgrimage or minor pilgrimage, let them walk between ˹the two hills˺. And whoever does good willingly, Allah is truly Appreciative, All-Knowing
phrases.ar: ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَنۡ حَجَّ ٱلۡبَيۡتَ أَوِ ٱعۡتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَاۚ وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرٗا فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
phrases.explanation:
The rite named is explained first. By Safa and Marwah are among the sacred symbols of Allah, Allah informed His believing servants that the running between the two is among the rites of the pilgrimage He instituted, which He commanded Abraham when he asked to be shown the rites. The form of the sentence is that of a statement, but what is intended is the command, since He made Abraham a leader for those who came after him, and so the command to follow him binds those who came after.

A view of the word for symbols is then set aside as far removed from what is understood.

The one who performs the lesser pilgrimage is then explained. He is called that only because, when he has gone around the House, he departs from it after his visit, and the word means the visit.

Then there is no blame upon him in going around the two is explained as meaning that there is no sin upon him in going around the two.

A recitation is rejected. Whoever distinguishes between the ruling of the two is asked for his proof, and the reading that has no blame upon him in not going around the two contradicts the codices of the Muslims.

The recitation of the last clause is then set out. Some of the reciters read it with the letter that makes it a completed act and others with the letter that makes it an effort, and both are correct and their meanings agree.

The correct view is then given. It is not the voluntary walking between the two, since one who walks between the two can only do so voluntarily in a pilgrimage, so what is meant is the voluntary performance of that pilgrimage.

phrases.translation: Those who hide the clear proofs and guidance that We have revealed—
phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡتُمُونَ مَآ أَنزَلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ وَٱلۡهُدَىٰ
phrases.explanation:
The ones described are explained first. By those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs, the sense is that the scholars of the Jews and their rabbis, and the scholars of the Christians, because of their concealing from the people the matter of the messenger and their refraining from following him, while they found him described in the Torah and the Gospel.

The clear proofs concealed are then named. It is that which was made clear concerning the matter of the messenger and his mission.

phrases.translation: after We made it clear for humanity in the Book—
phrases.ar: مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا بَيَّنَّٰهُ لِلنَّاسِ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ
phrases.explanation: The clause about making it clear is then explained. By after We have made it clear for the people in the Book, the sense is that a portion of the people, for the knowledge of the prophethood of the messenger, his description and his mission was only with the people of the book and with no one else, and they are the ones meant by the people of the book, and the book means the Torah and the Gospel.

phrases.translation: will be condemned by Allah and ˹all˺ those who condemn
phrases.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يَلۡعَنُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَيَلۡعَنُهُمُ ٱللَّٰعِنُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The guidance named is then explained. It is what was clarified to them of the matter of the messenger in the books sent down upon their prophets, so the verse refers to those who conceal from the people what was sent down in their books of clarification regarding the messenger, his prophethood, and the soundness of the community with which He sent him, without informing the people of it or making public what was clarified for them.

The curse named is then explained. By those are the ones whom Allah curses, these are the ones who conceal what Allah sent down concerning the messenger after He had made it clear to them in their books, and He curses them on account of their concealment and their refraining from making it clear.

The meaning of the verse is then given. They are the ones whom Allah removes from Himself and from His mercy, and the cursers ask their Lord to curse them, the cursing by the children of Adam being their saying, O Allah, curse him, since the curse means removal and driving away.

A question is then raised about who the cursers are, and it is noted that the plural of the beasts of the field is formed without the way it is formed for the children of Adam, so the reading cannot mean them.

The view preferred is then given. The cursers are the angels and the believers, since Allah described the disbelievers with the attribute that the curse upon them is from Allah, the angels and mankind together, and the curse reported upon the other group is of the same kind, and they are the cursers because both groups are people of disbelief.

phrases.translation: As for those who repent, mend their ways, and let the truth be known, they are the ones to whom I will turn ˹in forgiveness˺,
phrases.ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ تَابُواْ وَأَصۡلَحُواْ وَبَيَّنُواْ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَتُوبُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ
phrases.explanation:
The exception is explained first. By those who repent, and make it clear, the sense is that Allah and the cursers curse those who concealed from the people what they knew concerning the prophethood of the messenger, except the one among them who turns back from his concealment, who returns to repentance through faith in the messenger, who draws near to Allah with good deeds, and who makes clear what he knew of the revelation.

A claim is then rejected. It has been said that making it clear means that the repentance was made clear through sincerity of action, but the Book is against that.

Those concerned are named. They are Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions among the people of the book.

phrases.translation: for I am the Accepter of Repentance, Most Merciful
phrases.ar: وَأَنَا ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
phrases.explanation:
The closing words are then explained. By I am the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful, the sense is that He is the One who returns the hearts of His servants who have turned away from Him back to Him, and the Merciful toward those who turn to Him covers them with forgiveness.

A question is then raised. How can repentance be accepted from the one who has repented, and can there be one who repents without his repentance being accepted?

The answer is then given. This is a matter where one of the two cannot exist without the other accompanying it, so it is the same whether one says that the excepted are those whose repentance was accepted, or that they are those who repented, for indeed the acceptance of their repentance is announced.

phrases.translation: Surely those who disbelieve and die as disbelievers are condemned by Allah, the angels, and all of humanity
phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَمَاتُواْ وَهُمۡ كُفَّارٌ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ لَعۡنَةُ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ أَجۡمَعِينَ
phrases.explanation:
The people described are explained first. By those who disbelieve, the sense is those who denied the prophethood of the messenger and held him to be a liar, from among the Jews and the Christians and the rest of the adherents of religious communities, and the polytheists among the idol-worshippers. And die while they are disbelievers means they have died while persisting in that denial and their repudiation of the messenger.

The curse is then explained. Upon them is the curse of Allah and of the angels, meaning that upon those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers is the curse of Allah, for Allah has removed them far and distant from His mercy. And of the angels means that the angels and mankind together cursed them, and the cursing by the angels and mankind is their saying, upon them is the curse of Allah. The meaning of the curse was set forth earlier.

A disagreement is then recorded. Some of the exegetes said that by and of mankind all together, Allah meant the people who believe in Him and in His messenger, to the exclusion of the rest of mankind.

That is set aside, and other views are given instead. Some said this concerns the day of resurrection, when the disbeliever is placed before the heads of the witnesses and then all mankind curse him. Others said it concerns the saying of the speaker, may Allah curse the wrongdoer, and that then strikes every disbeliever.

The view preferred is then given. Allah meant all mankind, in the sense of their cursing of them through their saying, may Allah curse the wrongdoer.

phrases.translation: They will be in Hell forever. Their punishment will not be lightened,
phrases.ar: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا لَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنۡهُمُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ
phrases.explanation:
The clause is explained first. Abiding therein eternally means that they abide in the curse eternally, so that the punishment is not lightened for them and they are not granted respite to excuse themselves with an excuse.

A question is raised about the case of the word abiding, and the answer is given. It stands in the accusative as an adverbial qualifier of state, derived from the letters in the phrase upon them, since the meaning is that they are the ones whom Allah curses, and the angels, and mankind together.

A recitation is then mentioned and rejected. Although it is permissible in Arabic, it is not permitted to recite according to that reading, since it conflicts with the codices of the Muslims and the recitation they have transmitted by widespread dissemination.

phrases.translation: nor will they be delayed ˹from it˺
phrases.ar: وَلَا هُمۡ يُنظَرُونَ
phrases.explanation: A point of grammar is then added. The word for the curse is a verbal noun from the saying that Allah cursed him, in the meaning that He removes him and drives him away, and the same is meant by the cursing of the children of Adam, which is their saying, O Allah, curse him.

phrases.translation: Your God is ˹only˺ One God. There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him—the Most Compassionate, Most Merciful
phrases.ar: وَإِلَٰهُكُمۡ إِلَٰهٞ وَٰحِدٞۖ لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
phrases.explanation:
The statement is explained first. The meaning of godhood was expounded earlier, and it pertains to the worship rendered by created beings. By your god is one God, the sense is that He who has a right to your obedience and deserves worship from you is one worshipped one and one Lord, so worship none other than Him and set up no partner alongside Him.

The oneness is then explained further. Some said that the meaning of the oneness of Allah is the negating of any of His kind or equal to Him, as one says of a man that he is the only one among the people.

The proof that follows is then explained. By the verse that follows, Allah made known to the polytheists the place where the people of understanding could derive the proof for His oneness. So He said, if you are in doubt about that announcement, then ponder the proofs, for among them are the creation of the heavens and the earth, the alternation of night and day, the ships that sail upon the sea, the water sent down from the sky by which the earth is brought to life after its death, and the clouds made subservient between the heaven and the earth. If what you worship is able to create the like of any of that, then you would have an excuse for worshipping it besides Him, but if not, there is no excuse for you.

phrases.translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth; the alternation of the day and the night;
phrases.ar: إِنَّ فِي خَلۡقِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱخۡتِلَٰفِ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ
phrases.explanation:
The proof named first is examined. The alternation means the form derived from succeeding one another, whereby each of the two replaces the other, as He said that He made the night and the day a succession of one another for whoever wishes to remember or wishes to give thanks.

The creation is then named. By the creation of the heavens and the earth, the proof is set out at length, and it is explained that the denial of the disbelievers does not prevent everything He has mentioned being an indication of its Creator and Maker, which has a Governor equaled by nothing and a Producer who has no like.

The scope of the argument is then set out. He argued only against a people who acknowledged that Allah was their Creator, except that in His worship they ascribed partners through the worship of images and idols, so the argument was against those, and the sun and the moon running untiring in their course for the benefit of their sustenance is the meaning of the alternation of night and day, and the ships sailing on the sea with what benefits people is the meaning of the ships, and the rain sent down making their regions fertile after their dryness is the meaning of the water sent down from the sky, and the cattle made subservient to them upon the earth, in which there are foods and nourishment and beauty and mounts and clothing, is the meaning of the scattering of every kind of creature, and the fertilizing winds for the trees of their fruits and the clouds made subservient between the heaven and the earth are the meaning of the directing of the winds and the clouds.

phrases.translation: the ships that sail the sea for the benefit of humanity;
phrases.ar: وَٱلۡفُلۡكِ ٱلَّتِي تَجۡرِي فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ بِمَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ
phrases.explanation: The ships are then explained. By the ships that sail upon the sea with that which benefits mankind, the sense is indeed the ships that sail upon the sea, and these are counted among the proofs of the oneness of the Maker, since a ship is built and carried on the water and brings people what is of use to them, and it is one of the things He has made.

phrases.translation: the rain sent down by Allah from the skies, reviving the earth after its death; the scattering of all kinds of creatures throughout;
phrases.ar: وَمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مِن مَّآءٖ فَأَحۡيَا بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَا
phrases.explanation:
The water is then explained. By what Allah has sent down from the sky of water, the sense is the rain that Allah causes to descend from the sky.

The answer is then given at length. The denial of whoever denies does not prevent that everything He has mentioned is an indication of its Creator and Maker. The argument was against a people who acknowledged that Allah was their Creator, except that in His worship they ascribed partners through the worship of images and idols, so the rain sent down making the regions fertile after their dryness is the meaning of the water sent down from the sky, and the cattle made subservient to them, in which there are foods, mounts and clothing, is the meaning of the scattering of every kind of creature, and the fertilizing winds and the clouds are the last clause.

phrases.translation: the shifting of the winds;
phrases.ar: وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ دَآبَّةٖ
phrases.explanation:
The clause is then explained. By He scattered therein every kind of creature, the sense is in what He has scattered upon the earth of creatures.

Two points of grammar are then added. The word for scattered means distributed, derived from the saying of a commander who scattered his detachments of troops. And the word for creature is the active participle from the saying of a speaker that the creature crept with a creeping, and it is a designation for every animate being that is not a bird flying with its two wings, on account of its creeping over the earth.

phrases.translation: and the clouds drifting between the heavens and the earth—˹in all of this˺ are surely signs for people of understanding
phrases.ar: وَتَصۡرِيفِ ٱلرِّيَٰحِ وَٱلسَّحَابِ ٱلۡمُسَخَّرِ بَيۡنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ لَأٓيَٰتٖ لِّقَوۡمٖ يَعۡقِلُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The occasion of the verse is then discussed. Others said that it was sent down because the polytheists asked the messenger for a sign, so that they might be taught by it that in the creation of the heavens and the earth and all the rest mentioned with it lies a clear sign of the oneness of Allah and that He has no partner in His sovereignty, for whoever reflects with sound understanding.

The correct view is then given. Allah directed His servants by this verse to the demonstration of His oneness and His being alone in the divine kingship to the exclusion of all else. It is possible that it was sent down for one of the two views and possible that it was sent down for the other, and no report conclusively settles which is more correct, but whichever of the two is right, the intent of the verse is what has been said.

The closing clause is then explained. By the directing of the winds, the sense is the directing of the winds, and the agent was left out and the action attached to the object, as when one says it pleases me that your brother is honored, meaning your honoring of your brother. It is also possible that the meaning is the directing of the blowing of the wind through the variety of the places from which it blows.

The clouds and the signs are then explained. The cloud is called that because one part of it drags the other along. And the meaning of signs is marks and indications that the Creator of all this is one god.

phrases.translation: Still there are some who take others as Allah’s equal—
phrases.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَتَّخِذُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ
phrases.explanation:
The statement is explained first. The meaning of the verse is that among mankind there are those who take, besides Allah, equals to Him.

The word for equal was set forth earlier, meaning the peer, and the testimonies indicating that were given with it, so it is not repeated here.

phrases.translation: they love them as they should love Allah—but the ˹true˺ believers love Allah even more.
phrases.ar: أَندَادٗا يُحِبُّونَهُمۡ كَحُبِّ ٱللَّهِۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَشَدُّ حُبّٗا لِّلَّهِۗ
phrases.explanation:
The equals the people took are then discussed. The exegetes differed concerning them. Some of them said that they are their gods which they worshipped besides Allah, and the report naming who said that is given. Others said no, the equals here are rather their masters whom they obeyed in disobedience to Allah, and the report naming who said that is given.

The whole clause is then set out. The meaning is that among mankind are those who, O believers, take besides Allah equals whom they love as you love Allah.

The word for love is then explained, as one greets the emir, so they love them with the fullness of the love they have for Allah.

phrases.translation: If only the wrongdoers could see the ˹horrible˺ punishment ˹awaiting them˺,
phrases.ar: وَلَوۡ يَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. And if those who did wrong could see, it is stated that this is permissible when the word for indeed is put in the kasra as the opening of a new sentence, since the sense is if they could but know.

The reading preferred is then given. It is with the letter that makes it if you could see, and the sense is then you would see that the power belongs entirely to Allah and that Allah is severe in punishment, with the second clause omitted, since one contents oneself with the indication of the earlier words.

The reason for preferring it is then given. The people, when they see the punishment, already know with certainty that the power belongs entirely to Allah, so there is no basis for saying if they could but see, since that phrase is said only to one who has not seen.

The clause about beholding the punishment is then explained. It means when they see the punishment with their own eyes.

phrases.translation: they would certainly realize that all power belongs to Allah and that Allah is indeed severe in punishment
phrases.ar: إِذۡ يَرَوۡنَ ٱلۡعَذَابَ أَنَّ ٱلۡقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعٗا وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعَذَابِ
phrases.explanation:
The reciters differed concerning the recitation of this. The majority of the people of Medina and Syria recited it with the letter that makes it if you could see and with the fatḥa on the words for indeed, so that the sense is that if you could see those who did wrong when they behold the punishment, the power belongs entirely to Allah.

The case of the two words is then explained, that they stand in the accusative because of the omitted part of the phrase.

Other recitations are then set out. Some read the words for indeed with the kasra, so that the sense is that you would know the state into which they will come, and others read them with the letter that makes it if those who did wrong could see, so that the first of the two stands in the accusative because of the omitted answer, and the second is coupled to the first.

A grammatical claim is then mentioned, that the sense of that reading is if they could but know, since they did not know the extent of what they will behold.

phrases.translation: ˹Consider the Day˺ when those who misled others will disown their followers—when they face the torment—
phrases.ar: إِذۡ تَبَرَّأَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتُّبِعُواْ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُواْ وَرَأَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَ
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. By when those who were followed disavow those who followed them and they see the punishment, the sense is that when those who were followed disavow those who followed them and they see the punishment.

A disagreement is then recorded. The people of interpretation differed concerning whom is meant by this, and the reports of what they said are given.

The correct view is then given. Allah has announced that those who were followed in ascribing partners to Allah disavow their followers when they behold the punishment of Allah with their own eyes, and He did not single out some of them above others, but it comprises them all, so everyone who was followed in disbelief towards Allah disavows his followers who followed him in error.

The indication of the verse is then noted, which confirms the reading that the equals here are the men whom they obey and through whom they disobey Allah, and that the interpretation of those who said the ones disavowed are the devils falls away, since the verse stands in the context of the announcement concerning those who take equals.

phrases.translation: and the bonds that united them will be cut off
phrases.ar: وَتَقَطَّعَتۡ بِهِمُ ٱلۡأَسۡبَابُ
phrases.explanation:
The bonds are then explained. By the bonds between them are severed, the sense is that Allah is severe in punishment when those who were followed disavow and when the bonds between them are severed.

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of the bonds. Some of them said one thing, and others said that they are the abodes which they had among the people of this world, and the report naming who said that is given. And others said that the bonds are the deeds which they performed in this world.

The correct view is then given. Allah has announced that those who wronged themselves among the people of disbelief who died while they were disbelievers, that the followed one disavows the follower as soon as they behold the punishment of Allah with their own eyes, and that the bonds between them are severed.

The sense of the bonds is then explained further. All these are bonds by which one provides oneself in this world a means to one's desires, but Allah cut off their benefit in the hereafter for those who were disbelieving towards Him, because they were in conflict with His obedience, so their mutual friendship did not benefit them before their Lord, nor their worship of their equals, nor their obedience to their devils, and no kinship ties defended them against Allah's retribution, and their deeds did not benefit them but became grievous regret for them. Thus all the bonds of the disbelievers are severed.

phrases.translation: The ˹misled˺ followers will cry, “If only we could have a second chance, we would disown them as they disowned us.”
phrases.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُواْ لَوۡ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةٗ فَنَتَبَرَّأَ مِنۡهُمۡ كَمَا تَبَرَّءُواْ مِنَّاۗ
phrases.explanation: The followers are explained first. By those who followed will say, the sense is that the followers of those men, those whom they had taken as partners alongside Allah and obeyed in disobedience to Allah, will say, when they behold the punishment of Allah in the hereafter, if only we had a return, that is a second chance by which they might return to the worldly life.

phrases.translation: And so Allah will make them remorseful of their misdeeds.
phrases.ar: كَذَٰلِكَ يُرِيهِمُ ٱللَّهُ أَعۡمَٰلَهُمۡ حَسَرَٰتٍ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ
phrases.explanation:
Thus will Allah show them their deeds is explained first. The meaning is that just as He showed them the punishment which they denied in the worldly life, so too does He show them their corrupt deeds by which they deserved the punishment, as regrets for them, that is as remorseful feelings of regret.

The exegetes differed concerning the explanation of that. Some of them said that the meaning is that thus will Allah show them the deeds He prescribed for them in the worldly life but which they neglected and did not perform, until another through his obedience deserved what Allah had prepared for them, so that the reward that escaped them became for them grief and regret. Others said that thus will Allah show them their evil deeds as regrets for them, why did they do them, and why did they not do other deeds that please Allah.

The explanation preferred is then given. Thus will Allah show the disbelievers their corrupt deeds as regrets for them, why did they do them, and why did they not do others, so they feel regret over the evil deeds they committed when they see the requital of them from Allah.

A closing note is then added. What is most fitting is that to which the apparent meaning points and not that which the inner meaning might allow, since there is no indication that the inner sense is intended, and the apparent meaning of the revelation may not be turned away toward an inner interpretation.

phrases.translation: And they will never ˹be able to˺ leave the Fire
phrases.ar: وَمَا هُم بِخَٰرِجِينَ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ
phrases.explanation: The closing words are explained. By they will not depart from the Fire, the sense is that these disbelievers, even though they feel remorse after beholding the punishment with their own eyes, so that their regret became intense and they wished for a return to the worldly life in order to repent therein and disavow those who misled them, will not depart from the Fire in which Allah made them burn on account of their disbelief, and their regret there will not save them at that moment, but therein they will abide forever.

phrases.translation: O humanity! Eat from what is lawful and good on the earth and do not follow Satan’s footsteps.
phrases.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ كُلُواْ مِمَّا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ حَلَٰلٗا طَيِّبٗا وَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ خُطُوَٰتِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِۚ
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. By eat of what is on the earth lawful and good, the address is to all people.

The footsteps of the devil are then discussed. The scholars of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of that phrase. Some of them said that the footsteps of the devil are his work, and the other sayings reported are close to one another in meaning, since each of them pointed to the prohibition of following the devil in his tracks and his deeds. The proper meaning of the word is then given, that it is the distance between his two feet, and it is then used for all his tracks and paths.

phrases.translation: He is truly your sworn enemy
phrases.ar: إِنَّهُۥ لَكُمۡ عَدُوّٞ مُّبِينٌ
phrases.explanation:
The address is then explained in full. Eat of the foodstuffs that have been made lawful for you through the tongue of the messenger and thereby made good for you, and not of that which has been forbidden, such as carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that over which another than Allah has been invoked. And abandon the footsteps of the devil, who ruins you and forbids you your own possessions.
