The devil is then described. Truly he is to you a manifest enemy, for he has made his enmity to you manifest through his refusal to prostrate before your father and his deception of him until he caused him to be expelled from the garden.

The two words are then explained. Lawful means released, and good means pure, neither impure nor forbidden.

phrases.translation: He only incites you to commit evil and indecency, and to claim against Allah what you do not know
phrases.ar: إِنَّمَا يَأۡمُرُكُم بِٱلسُّوٓءِ وَٱلۡفَحۡشَآءِ وَأَن تَقُولُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. It continues the prohibition of following the footsteps of the devil, and by He only commands you the sense is that the devil commands you to do evil and the shameful and to say about Allah what you do not know.

The two words are then explained. Evil means sin, comparable to harm, derived from the saying of a person that a matter grieved him, so it is that which inflicts suffering upon the one who does it. And the shameful is a verbal noun, comparable to prosperity and adversity, and it is everything whose mention is regarded as shameful and whose hearing is detestable.

phrases.translation: When it is said to them, “Follow what Allah has revealed,” they reply, “No! We ˹only˺ follow what we found our forefathers practicing.”
phrases.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱتَّبِعُواْ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ قَالُواْ بَلۡ نَتَّبِعُ مَآ
phrases.explanation:
The pronoun is then discussed. The first view is that the pronoun in and when it is said to them refers back to those among the people who take besides Allah equals, so that the meaning would be that among the people are those who take equals, and when it is said to them, follow what Allah has sent down, they say, no, we follow that upon which we found our forefathers.

The view preferred is then given. The pronoun refers to the people, and this is a return from direct address to a report about an absent party, since it comes directly after the address to people, and the account about the ones who take equals is interrupted by a new and different account, and the verse was sent down concerning the Arabs of the age of ignorance who forbade for themselves what they forbade.

The command is then explained. Follow what Allah has sent down means act according to what Allah has sent down in His Book to His messenger, so declare lawful what He makes lawful and forbid what He forbids, and take him as a leader whom you follow.

phrases.translation: ˹Would they still do so,˺ even if their forefathers had ˹absolutely˺ no understanding or guidance
phrases.ar: أَلۡفَيۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَنَآۚ أَوَلَوۡ كَانَ ءَابَآؤُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡقِلُونَ شَيۡـٔٗا وَلَا يَهۡتَدُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The whole verse is then set out. And when it is said to these unbelievers, eat of what Allah has made lawful for you and leave the footsteps of Satan behind you, then they show arrogance and refuse to submit to the truth, and they say, no, we follow the example of our forefathers, namely the making lawful of what they made lawful and the forbidding of what they forbade.

The closing clause is then explained. Even though their forefathers were, meaning the forefathers of these unbelievers who have passed away in their disbelief, who understood nothing of the religion of Allah nor of His obligations, command and prohibition, so that they should be followed upon the path they trod, and who were not guided to the right path, so that others would let themselves be guided by them?

phrases.translation: The example of the disbelievers ˹not responding to the Messenger’s warning˺ is like a flock not comprehending the calls and cries of the shepherd.
phrases.ar: وَمَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ كَمَثَلِ ٱلَّذِي يَنۡعِقُ بِمَا لَا يَسۡمَعُ إِلَّا دُعَآءٗ وَنِدَآءٗۚ
phrases.explanation: The first interpretation is then given. The meaning of this is that the likeness of the disbeliever, in his scant understanding of what Allah lays before him in His Book and in his poor acceptance of that to which he is called, namely the profession of the oneness of Allah and that of which he is admonished, is as the likeness of the head of cattle that hears the sound when it is called out to but does not understand what is said to it.

phrases.translation: ˹They are wilfully˺ deaf, dumb and blind so they have no understanding
phrases.ar: صُمُّۢ بُكۡمٌ عُمۡيٞ فَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡقِلُونَ
phrases.explanation:
Another interpretation is then given. The likeness of those who disbelieve in their invoking of their gods and their idols, which neither hear nor understand, is as the likeness of one who calls out to something that hears nothing but a shout and a call, and that is the echo, of which he hears only the sound without the caller perceiving anything from it.

The interpretation preferred is then given. It is the first, namely that the likeness of the admonition of the disbeliever and his admonisher is as the likeness of one who calls out to his flock and his calling them thereto, for it hears his calling out but does not understand his words.

A point of grammar is then added, that the omission of the word for admonition is permissible, with the likeness serving as a sufficient substitute for it.

The reason for choosing this interpretation is then given. The verse was revealed concerning the Jews, who were not adherents of idols that they worshipped nor of false gods, and the evidence is the verses that precede it and that follow it, so it is more fitting that what lies between them be a report about them.

The closing words are then explained. By deaf, dumb and blind, the sense is that they are deaf to the truth so that they do not hear it, dumb in that they are speechless with respect to proclaiming the truth and making clear the matter of the messenger, and blind to the guidance and the path of the truth, so that they do not see it.

A point of grammar is then added. The nominative in those words accrues on account of the beginning of a new sentence and the resumption, as one says in common usage, he is deaf, he does not hear.

phrases.translation: O believers! Eat from the good things We have provided for you. And give thanks to Allah if you ˹truly˺ worship Him ˹alone˺
phrases.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُلُواْ مِن طَيِّبَٰتِ مَا رَزَقۡنَٰكُمۡ وَٱشۡكُرُواْ لِلَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ إِيَّاهُ تَعۡبُدُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The address is explained first. By O you who believe, the sense is those who have held Allah and His messenger to be true, who have surrendered themselves to servitude before Allah, and who have submitted to Him.

The command is then explained. Eat of the good things with which We have provided you means eat of the permitted provision which has been made lawful for you and became good for you, namely of that which you yourselves declared forbidden though it had not been forbidden to you. And be grateful to Allah means praise Allah for that to which He has a right from your side, on account of the blessings He has provided you. If it is truly Him whom you worship means if you submit to His command and are obedient, then eat of what He has made lawful and abandon the footsteps of Satan.

phrases.translation: He has only forbidden you ˹to eat˺ carrion, blood, swine, and what is slaughtered in the name of any other than Allah.
phrases.ar: إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡمَيۡتَةَ وَٱلدَّمَ وَلَحۡمَ ٱلۡخِنزِيرِ وَمَآ أُهِلَّ بِهِۦ لِغَيۡرِ ٱللَّهِۖ
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. He has only forbidden you the carrion and the blood and the flesh of swine and that over which at the slaughtering a name other than that of Allah has been invoked. The sense given is that the believers are not to forbid for themselves what has not been forbidden them, such as the animals dedicated to idols, but rather to eat, for nothing has been forbidden them except those four things.

A point of grammar is then given. The word for only is a single particle, and for that reason the carrion and the blood stand in the accusative, and no other case is permissible with the carrion when the word is taken as a single particle. But if it were two particles, then the carrion would stand in the nominative, and the meaning of the sentence would be that what Allah has forbidden you of foods is the carrion, the blood and the flesh of swine and nothing other than that.

Some of the reciters did recite it thus, and it is not permissible to recite that way even though it has an intelligible ground, because of the agreement of the reciters upon the contrary, and no one may object to them in what they have transmitted in unanimity.

Two further possibilities are then set out if the word for forbidden is read in the passive form, and both are set aside for the same reason.

The correct judgment is then given. The lightening and the doubling in the letter are two well-known forms, both in recitation and in the speech of the Arabs, and with whichever of the two a reciter recites it he is correct, since there is no difference in the meaning.

The last item is then explained. That over which at the slaughtering a name other than that of Allah has been invoked means that which is slaughtered for the false deities and the idols.

phrases.translation: But if someone is compelled by necessity—neither driven by desire nor exceeding immediate need—they will not be sinful.
phrases.ar: فَمَنِ ٱضۡطُرَّ غَيۡرَ بَاغٖ وَلَا عَادٖ فَلَآ إِثۡمَ عَلَيۡهِۚ
phrases.explanation:
The exception is explained first. By but whoever is compelled by necessity, the sense is that whoever is driven by the necessity of hunger to that which has been forbidden, and is in the condition described, has no sin upon him in eating it if he eats it.

A point of grammar is then given. The phrase without being desirous stands in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier for whoever, so the sense is that whoever is compelled without being desirous and without transgressing and then eats it, for him that is permitted. And it has also been said that the meaning is whoever is forced to eat it and then eats it, upon him is no sin.

The two phrases are then discussed. Some said that without being desirous or transgressing means without desiring the forbidden in his eating and without overstepping the limit of what is permitted him of the forbidden. Others said that it means without desiring it out of appetite and without overstepping the limit beyond what is indispensable for him.

The statement preferred is then given. Whoever is compelled by necessity, without being desirous by eating that which it is forbidden for him to eat, and without overstepping the limit in his eating, while he has the possibility and the capacity to refrain from eating it because of something else that Allah has permitted him.

The word for transgressing is then examined. It has been said that it means without eating so much that he becomes sated but only as much as keeps him alive, and that is one of the meanings of transgressing, for Allah has not excepted any particular meaning of it.

The closing words are then explained. Upon him is no sin means that whoever eats that in the condition described has no liability for so eating it and no fault.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٞ رَّحِيمٌ
phrases.explanation: The closing words are explained. By Allah is Forgiving, Merciful, the sense is that Allah overlooks what has gone before from error, sin and disobedience in the time of ignorance, if you obey Allah in your Islam, abstain from eating what He has forbidden you, and leave off following Satan in that which you held forbidden in that time, and He is merciful toward you if you obey Him.

phrases.translation: Indeed, those who hide Allah’s revelations, trading them for a fleeting gain consume nothing but fire into their bellies.
phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡتُمُونَ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَيَشۡتَرُونَ بِهِۦ ثَمَنٗا قَلِيلًا
phrases.explanation:
The people described are explained first. By those who conceal what Allah has sent down of the Book, the sense is the scribes of the Jews, who concealed from the people the matter of the messenger and his prophethood while they found it recorded in the Torah, in exchange for bribes they received for that.

The phrase about the price is then explained. And sell it for a paltry price means they purchase something with it, and the meaning is that with their concealing of what they concealed regarding the matter of the messenger they purchased a paltry price, since what they received for distorting the Book of Allah and explaining it in an incorrect manner was only paltry worldly goods.

phrases.translation: Allah will neither speak to them on the Day of Judgment, nor will He purify them. And they will suffer a painful punishment
phrases.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ مَا يَأۡكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمۡ إِلَّا ٱلنَّارَ وَلَا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَلَا يُزَكِّيهِمۡ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
phrases.explanation:
The first half is explained at length. Those who conceal what Allah has sent down of the Book regarding the matter of the messenger in exchange for the wretched bribery given to them, for which they distort the signs of Allah and alter their meanings, eat nothing in their bellies, through their eating of the bribes they took and the promised wage, but the Fire, that is to say, nothing but that which causes them to enter the Fire and to burn therein, just as He has said that those who unjustly devour the property of orphans only devour fire in their bellies. He thus contented Himself with the mention of the Fire and the understanding of the listeners.

The closing clause is then explained. Nor purify them means nor purify them of the defilement of their sins and their disbelief, and for them is a painful punishment means an agonizing one.

phrases.translation: They are the ones who trade guidance for misguidance and forgiveness for punishment.
phrases.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱشۡتَرَوُاْ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةَ بِٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَٱلۡعَذَابَ بِٱلۡمَغۡفِرَةِۚ
phrases.explanation: The clause is explained at length. By those are they who have purchased error for guidance and chastisement for forgiveness, the sense is that they are those who have taken error and abandoned guidance, and who have taken that which makes them deserve the chastisement of Allah on the day of resurrection, and who have abandoned that which would make them deserve His forgiveness and good pleasure. He contented Himself with mentioning the chastisement and the forgiveness without naming the cause that brings about deserving these two, because those who hear it understand its meaning, and the import of the phrase was expounded earlier.

phrases.translation: How persistent are they in pursuit of the Fire
phrases.ar: فَمَآ أَصۡبَرَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ
phrases.explanation:
The sentence is discussed. The people of interpretation differed concerning the explanation of it. Some of them said that the meaning is how audacious they are in performing the deed that brings them near to the Fire. Others said that it is an exclamation of wonder, how intense is their audacity toward the Fire through their performing the deeds of the people of the Fire.

The explanation of each is then given. For those who read it as an exclamation of wonder, the sense is how intense is their audacity, through their performing what they have performed, toward that which makes them deserve the Fire, just as He said, cursed be man, how ungrateful he is, as an exclamation of wonder at his disbelief in the One who created him. For those who read it as a question, the sense is what makes them steadfast toward the Fire, while no one has steadfastness toward the Fire, until they have exchanged it for the forgiveness of Allah.

The view preferred is then given. How audacious they are toward the chastisement of the Fire, and how greatly they perform the deeds of its inhabitants, and the reason is that it has been transmitted from the Arabs, how audacious is so-and-so toward Allah, and Allah causes His creatures to wonder only through making manifest the report about those who conceal what He has sent down, and about their purchasing a paltry price of bribes, by way of wonder at their audacity toward that despite their knowledge that it makes them deserve His wrath.

A closing note is then added. One contented oneself with mentioning the Fire without naming its chastisement, as one says how greatly your generosity resembles that of Hatim.

phrases.translation: That is because Allah has revealed the Book in truth. And surely those who differ regarding it are totally engrossed in opposition
phrases.ar: ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ نَزَّلَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّۗ وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَفِي شِقَاقِۭ بَعِيدٖ
phrases.explanation:
The reference is discussed first. There was disagreement over what is meant by that.

One view is then given. That means the deed of theirs, namely their audacity in the face of the punishment of the Fire and their concealing what Allah sent down concerning the messenger, and this is because Allah sent down the Book with the truth.

Another view is given, that that is known to them, because We have informed in the Book that this holds for them.

The view preferred is then given. That refers to all that the statement comprised, of His informing about the deeds of the rabbis of the Jews and what He has prepared for them of punishment, so this which they did is because I sent down My Book with the truth.

A point of grammar is then added. For that there are two case endings, the nominative by means of the particle and the accusative in the sense of I did that because, and their disbelief was left out.

The second half is then explained. By those who differed concerning the Book, the sense is the Jews and the Christians, who differed concerning the Book of Allah, the Jews disbelieving in what Allah related therein concerning Jesus and his mother, and all of them disbelieving in the command to hold the messenger true, so they are in a dispute far removed from the truth.

phrases.translation: Righteousness is not in turning your faces towards the east or the west. Rather, the righteous are those who believe in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Books, and the prophets;
phrases.ar: لَّيۡسَ ٱلۡبِرَّ أَن تُوَلُّواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ قِبَلَ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ وَٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلۡبِرَّ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ وَٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ وَءَاتَى
phrases.explanation:
The meaning of the verse is discussed. The scholars of interpretation differed. Some of them said that piety is not the prayer alone but consists of the qualities that are set forth in the verse. Others said that Allah meant the Jews and the Christians, since the Jews pray turning toward the west and the Christians turning toward the east, so the verse informs them that piety is not the deed they perform but what is set forth in it.

The view preferred is then given. It is that of Qatada and al-Rabi ibn Anas, namely that the Jews and the Christians are meant, since the verses before it have already rebuked them and informed them of the punishment prepared for them. So piety is not, O Jews and Christians, that some of you turn toward the east and some toward the west, but pious is he who believes in Allah and the last day and the angels and the book.

A further point is then added. It is also possible that the meaning is that pious is he who believes in Allah, in which case the word for piety would be a verbal noun in the position of the agent.

phrases.translation: who give charity out of their cherished wealth to relatives, orphans, the poor, ˹needy˺ travellers, beggars, and for freeing captives;
phrases.ar: ٱلۡمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ ذَوِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينَ وَٱبۡنَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَٱلسَّآئِلِينَ وَفِي
phrases.explanation:
The giving is explained first. By and who gives wealth in spite of his love for it, the sense is that he gave his wealth at the moment of his love for it, his greed with it and his stinginess over it.

The wayfarer is then explained. It is the one who passes by the man while traveling, and the scholars differed about his description, some of them saying that he is the guest.

Another view is then given. The first wealth is the alms-tax, but Allah described the giving by the believers to those to whom they gave it, so He made known the places where they must spend their alms, and then indicated that the wealth the people gave is the obligatory alms-tax.

The fulfilling of covenants is then explained. And those who fulfill their covenant when they make a covenant means those who do not break the covenant of Allah after making it, but fulfill it and complete it in accordance with that over which they made it.

A long grammatical argument is then given. It has been claimed that those who are patient in adversity stand in the accusative as a conjunction to the beggars, but the clear text of the Book shows that this is wrong, since those patient in adversity and distress are the people with chronic ailments and with straitened means, and the description of the people to whom they give has already preceded in the mention of the needy, the wayfarer and the beggars, so making it a repetition would have no point. Rather, pious is he who believes in Allah and the last day, and those who fulfill their covenant, and those patient in adversity and distress.

phrases.translation: who establish prayer, pay alms-tax, and keep the pledges they make;
phrases.ar: ٱلرِّقَابِ وَأَقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَى ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلۡمُوفُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The freeing of slaves is then explained. By and for the freeing of necks, the sense is the freeing of necks from slavery, and these are the contract-slaves who strive to free their necks by fulfilling their manumission contracts, on the basis of which they are separated from their masters.

The prayer and the alms-tax are then explained. By and who performs the prayer, the sense is that he performed it constantly with its conditions, and by and who gives the alms-tax, that he gave it as Allah has prescribed it for him.

phrases.translation: and who are patient in times of suffering, adversity, and in ˹the heat of˺ battle. It is they who are true ˹in faith˺,
phrases.ar: بِعَهۡدِهِمۡ إِذَا عَٰهَدُواْۖ وَٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ فِي ٱلۡبَأۡسَآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ وَحِينَ ٱلۡبَأۡسِۗ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ
phrases.explanation:
The meaning is then given. And those who restrain themselves, in adversity and in distress and in the hour of battle, from that which Allah disapproves of for them, and who hold the soul fast to that which He has commanded them of obedience to Him.

The phrase is then examined. The grammarians differed about it, some of them saying that adversity and distress is a verbal noun that has come upon the pattern of the broken plural and has no form of the sound plural, since it is a noun, and they have used the sound plural in the qualifier without its taking the broken plural form.

A point of grammar is then added. The phrase lion of the battle-array and man of insight is placed in the accusative in the manner of praise, while the noun before it was in the genitive, because it was a qualification of the singular.

The hour of battle is then explained. It means the time of the intensity of armed combat in war.

A description of war is then given, that war is impregnated as the she-camel is impregnated and brings forth twins in one belly, and the ruddy one of Ad is explained as the ruddy one of Thamud, who hamstrung the she-camel of Allah, whereupon their Lord destroyed them, and that war suckles her offspring and tends them until she weans them.

phrases.translation: and it is they who are mindful ˹of Allah˺
phrases.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُواْۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُتَّقُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The interpretation of the verse is then given. And who gave wealth, while he loves it, is covetous of amassing it and is stingy with it, to his kinsfolk, and thereby maintained the ties of kinship with them.

The truthful ones are then explained. By those are the ones who were truthful, the sense is the one who believed in Allah and the last day and whom He described with the description with which He described them in this verse, so whoever performs these things, those are the ones who were faithful to Allah in their faith and realized their word with their deeds, and not the one who turns his face toward the east and the west while opposing Allah in His command, breaking His covenant and agreement, concealing from the people the exposition of what Allah has commanded him to make clear, and denying His messengers.

The God-fearing are then explained. And those are the ones who feared the punishment of Allah and therefore avoided disobedience to Him and dreaded His threat, so they did not transgress His limits, and they feared Him and therefore performed the observance of His obligations.

phrases.translation: O believers! ˹The law of˺ retaliation is set for you in cases of murder—a free man for a free man, a slave for a slave, and a female for a female.
phrases.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡقِصَاصُ فِي ٱلۡقَتۡلَىۖ ٱلۡحُرُّ بِٱلۡحُرِّ وَٱلۡعَبۡدُ بِٱلۡعَبۡدِ وَٱلۡأُنثَىٰ بِٱلۡأُنثَىٰۚ
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. Retaliation for the slain is prescribed for you, the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female, and the sense is that it is made obligatory upon you.

An objection is then answered. When a free person kills a free person, then the blood of the killer is an equivalent for the blood of the slain, and the retaliation strikes him and no one else, so do not transgress toward another who did not kill.

The people differed about the occasion of the verse. Some of them said that it was revealed concerning a people who were not content with the blood of a slave for their slain one until they killed his master, and not content with the blood of a woman until they killed a man of her tribe. Others said that it was revealed concerning two groups who fought one another in the time of the messenger, and the prophet commanded that peace be made between them. Others said that it is a command to offset the blood money of the free, the slave, the man and the woman with mutual reckoning of the difference.

The ruling that the verse indicates is then applied. The reports of the messenger reinforce one another that the life of the free man is offset by way of retaliation against the life of the free woman, and it is agreed by all Muslims that it is forbidden for a man to destroy a limb of his body for a compensation, so it is obligatory that the life of the free man serve as retaliation for the life of the free woman.

All are agreed without exception that the mutual reckoning of rights is not obligatory, and that Allah has pronounced no ruling therein that He then abrogated, so the correct view is the one that has been voiced.

A point of grammar is then added. The word for the slain is the plural of the slain one, and the mention of is subjected to retaliation was omitted because the indication of retaliation is prescribed for you sufficed.

phrases.translation: But if the offender is pardoned by the victim’s guardian,
phrases.ar: فَمَنۡ عُفِيَ لَهُۥ مِنۡ أَخِيهِ شَيۡءٞ
phrases.explanation:
It has also been said that the meaning of retaliation in this verse is the mutual offsetting of the blood money of some of the slain against that of others.

The exegetes differed over the clause whoever is pardoned something by his brother, and some of them said that it means whoever of the killing that was unlawful is remitted something of the retaliation.

A further view is then given from the interpretation transmitted from Ali and al-Hasan, namely that whoever is remitted that which was obligatory upon him for his brother of the retaliation of the blood money of one against that of the other, then there is a demand by the next of kin and a payment by the killer.

The view preferred is then given. Whoever is remitted that which was obligatory upon him for his brother of retaliation, for a blood money that he accepts, then there is a demand in a fitting manner and a payment by the killer in a good manner.

phrases.translation: then blood-money should be decided fairly
phrases.ar: فَٱتِّبَاعُۢ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَأَدَآءٌ إِلَيۡهِ بِإِحۡسَٰنٖۗ
phrases.explanation:
By then let there be a fitting demand, the sense is that there is a demand for what Allah has granted him as a right against the killer of his kinsman, without his being charged with more than what he is entitled to regarding the ages of the blood-money camels.

A point of grammar is then added. Some of the philologists said that its nominative rests on the meaning that upon the one who is pardoned something by his brother rests a fitting demand, and that is the view held here, whereas in the phrase then strike the necks the accusative is correct, because it is an exhortation to kill upon meeting the enemy.

phrases.translation: and payment should be made courteously. This is a concession and a mercy from your Lord.
phrases.ar: ذَٰلِكَ تَخۡفِيفٞ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ وَرَحۡمَةٞۗ
phrases.explanation:
That is a lightening from your Lord and a mercy is explained. By that, the sense is this concerning which I have ruled and prescribed for you, namely My permitting you to refrain from retaliation upon the killer of your slain one for a blood money that you accept, which I had forbidden to the communities before you, so it is a lightening from Me and mercy for you.

The reading of those who say that retaliation here is the offsetting of the blood monies is then explained, that this which I have done with you is a lightening from Me of the heaviness of what rested upon you, and mercy for you.

phrases.translation: But whoever transgresses after that will suffer a painful punishment
phrases.ar: فَمَنِ ٱعۡتَدَىٰ بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ فَلَهُۥ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٞ
phrases.explanation:
But whoever transgresses after that is explained. Whoever transgresses what Allah has granted him, after he has accepted the blood money, by way of transgression and injustice toward what He has not appointed for him, namely the killing of the killer of his kinsman and the shedding of his blood, for him is a painful punishment.

The exegetes differed concerning that punishment. Some of them said that it is the killing of him as retaliation for the one he killed after the acceptance of the blood money from him. And some of them said that it is a chastisement with which the ruler punishes him, according to the measure of what he deems fitting.

phrases.translation: There is ˹security of˺ life for you in ˹the law of˺ retaliation,
phrases.ar: وَلَكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡقِصَاصِ حَيَوٰةٞ
phrases.explanation:
The clause is explained first. By and in legal retaliation there is life for you, O people of insight, the sense is that for you, O people of understanding, there is in that which I have prescribed for you, namely retaliation in cases of killing, wounds and head injuries, that which restrains some of you from killing others and through which some of you refrain from others, so you remained alive thereby. So in My judgment, by which I judged between you, there is life for you.

The scholars of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of this, and some of them said something along the lines of what has been said about it, and the report naming who said that is given.

Another view is then given. The meaning is that in legal retaliation against the killer there is a continued existence for others, because according to the judgment of Allah, for the one killed none is killed except his killer, whereas in the time of ignorance they would kill for the woman the man, and for the slave the free man.

phrases.translation: O people of reason, so that you may become mindful ˹of Allah˺
phrases.ar: يَٰٓأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The address is then explained. O people of insight means O people of understanding, and the word for minds is the plural of the intellect. And the address is directed specifically to the people of understanding, because they are the ones who comprehend the command and prohibition of Allah and reflect upon His signs and proofs, unlike others.

The closing clause is then explained. So that you may become God-fearing means so that you may fear retaliation and thereby refrain from killing.

phrases.translation: It is prescribed that when death approaches any of you—if they leave something of value—a will should be made in favour of parents and immediate family with fairness.
phrases.ar: كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ إِن تَرَكَ خَيۡرًا ٱلۡوَصِيَّةُ لِلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبِينَ
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. It is prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you and he leaves behind good, to make a bequest in favor of the parents and the nearest relatives in a fitting manner, a duty upon the God-fearing.

The correct view is then given. It is that of al-Zuhri, for both little property and much property fall under the designation of good, and Allah did not specify it by a limit nor except anything from it, so that it would not be permissible to divert the outward meaning toward a hidden one. So everyone whose death approaches while he has property, little or much, is obligated to make a bequest from it in favor of whoever among his fathers, mothers and nearest relatives does not inherit from him, in a fitting manner.

phrases.translation: ˹This is˺ an obligation on those who are mindful ˹of Allah˺
phrases.ar: بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِۖ حَقًّا عَلَى ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
phrases.explanation:
By it is prescribed for you, the sense is that it is imposed upon you as a duty, the bequest, when death approaches one of you and he leaves behind good, in favor of the parents and the nearest relatives who do not inherit from him, in a fitting manner, that is in the manner that Allah has permitted, namely that which does not exceed the third part, and a duty upon the God-fearing means that this is imposed upon you for whoever fears Allah and obeys Him.

A question is then raised. Is it an obligation upon the man who possesses property to make a bequest in favor of his parents and nearest relatives who do not inherit from him?

The answer is then given. He has made known to us that He has prescribed it and imposed it as a duty, just as He says fasting is prescribed for you, and there is no disagreement that whoever neglects fasting while able to do so has neglected a duty of Allah, and likewise whoever neglects the bequest while he possesses something concerning which he can make it is one who neglects a duty of Allah.

A group then contradicts this. It is a firmly established verse, not abrogated, and when there is disagreement among the scholars about its abrogation it is not permissible to rule that it is abrogated except on the basis of a proof to which one must submit, since it is not impossible that the ruling of this verse and the ruling of the verse concerning the shares of inheritance coexist in one situation, the one annulling the other.

Others said that it is a verse by which the ruling was obligatory and acted upon for a time, and then the verse concerning the shares of inheritance abrogated the bequest in favor of the parents and nearest relatives who do inherit, while the obligation remained for those who do not inherit. And others said that Allah abrogated all of it and made the shares of inheritance obligatory, so that no bequest is obligatory for anyone.

phrases.translation: But whoever changes the will after hearing it, the blame will only be on those who made the change. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.ar: فَمَنۢ بَدَّلَهُۥ بَعۡدَ مَا سَمِعَهُۥ فَإِنَّمَآ إِثۡمُهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُبَدِّلُونَهُۥٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٞ
phrases.explanation:
The clause is explained first. By whoever alters it after he has heard it, the sense is that whoever alters what the testator has left as a bequest, from his lawful disposition, then the sin of that alteration rests upon whoever alters it.

A question is then raised about what the word in whoever alters it refers back to, and the answer is that it refers back to something omitted from the words, namely the matter of the deceased.

The closing words are explained. By Allah is All-Hearing, the sense is that Allah hears the bequest, whether you act justly in it or deviate from the truth, and All-Knowing of what your breasts conceal.

phrases.translation: Whoever suspects an error or an injustice in the will and brings about a ˹fair˺ settlement among the parties will not be sinful. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.ar: فَمَنۡ خَافَ مِن مُّوصٖ جَنَفًا أَوۡ إِثۡمٗا فَأَصۡلَحَ بَيۡنَهُمۡ فَلَآ إِثۡمَ عَلَيۡهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٞ رَّحِيمٞ
phrases.explanation:
The people differed about the meaning of the verse. Some of them said that it is whoever is present with a sick person at the threshold of death who fears that the sick man is committing an error in his will or deliberately intending injustice in it, so there is no objection to the one who brings about reconciliation between him and his heirs by enjoining justice in his will. Others said that it is whoever, from among the kinsfolk of the deceased or the one in authority over the affairs of the Muslims, fears partiality in the will and brings about reconciliation between the heirs and those for whom the will is made. And others said that it is whoever fears partiality in favour of some of his parents and relatives at the expense of others, and brings about reconciliation between the parents and the relatives.

The most correct of these statements is then given. Whoever fears from a testator partiality or sin, namely that he deviates by an error on his part to something other than the truth, or that he deliberately intends a sin in his will, by making a will in favor of his parents and near relatives who do not inherit from him for more than is permitted him to leave to them, or that he exceeds the third or leaves the entire third while there is little property and many heirs, then there is no objection upon the one who is present with him that he brings about reconciliation between those for whom the will is made and the deceased, by enjoining upon the deceased what is fitting and acquainting him with what Allah has allowed him, and forbidding him from exceeding what is fitting.

The reason for this choice is then given. It has been preferred only because He said, whoever fears from a testator partiality or sin, meaning whoever fears from a testator that he will be partial or will sin, for the fear of partiality and sin exists only before their occurrence, and had that been the meaning it would have been said whoever ascertains from a testator partiality or sin.

A question is then raised about what bringing about reconciliation means, since reconciliation only takes place between people who disagree.

The recitation of the phrase is then noted, that it is recited with the lightening of the letter and the quieting of the vowel, and with the movement of the vowel and the doubling of the letter.

The sense of the words is then given, and the closing words are explained. By Allah is Forgiving, Merciful, the sense is that Allah is forgiving toward the testator for that to which he had incited himself of partiality and sin when he refrains from sinning in his will, and merciful toward the one who brings about reconciliation between the testator and the one against whom he wished to commit injustice in favour of another.

phrases.translation: O believers!
phrases.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا
phrases.explanation: The address is explained first. By O you who believe, the sense is those who believe in Allah and His messenger and who have affirmed and acknowledged them both. And by fasting is prescribed for you, the sense is that fasting is made obligatory upon you.

phrases.translation: Fasting is prescribed for you—as it was for those before you—so perhaps you will become mindful ˹of Allah˺
phrases.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The word for fasting is then examined. It is a verbal noun, from the saying of a person that I abstained from it, and its meaning is abstaining from that which Allah has commanded one to abstain from, and it is also said that the horses fasted when they ceased from travelling, and a line of poetry is cited as a witness for that sense.

The comparison with those before is then explained. As it was prescribed for those before you means it is made obligatory upon you equal to that which was made obligatory upon them.

The exegetes differed concerning whom is meant by those before you and in what sense the comparison was made.

One answer is then given, that the comparison is only because their fasting was from the evening prayer to the evening prayer, which was the obligation upon the believers when fasting was first made obligatory, and those who held this agreed that those meant are the Christians. Others said that those meant are the people of the book.

The closing words are then explained. That you may become God-fearing means that you may abstain from eating food, drinking drink and intercourse with women in it, so fasting is made obligatory upon you that you may abstain from what breaks your fast during the time of your fasting.

phrases.translation: ˹Fast a˺ prescribed number of days. But whoever of you is ill or on a journey, then ˹let them fast˺ an equal number of days ˹after Ramaḍân˺.
phrases.ar: أَيَّامٗا مَّعۡدُودَٰتٖۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٖ فَعِدَّةٞ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۚ
phrases.explanation:
The first clause is explained first. Prescribed for you is fasting for a number of appointed days. The word for days stands in the accusative because of an elided verb, and the phrase as it was prescribed for those before you pertains to the fasting itself.

The view preferred is then given. Allah meant by the days of appointed days the days of the month of Ramadan, because no report has come upon which a proof can be founded that the people of Islam were prescribed any fasting other than that of Ramadan, and because in the context of the verse Allah has made clear that the fasting He has made obligatory is that of Ramadan and no other. So whoever claims they were charged with another fasting is asked for its proof, since it can only be known through a report that cuts off excuse.

The second clause is then explained. Whoever of you is sick or on a journey, then a number of other days, meaning that upon him rests the fasting of the days that he broke during his illness or on his journey, on other days.

phrases.translation: For those who can only fast with extreme difficulty, compensation can be made by feeding a needy person ˹for every day not fasted˺. But whoever volunteers to give more, it is better for them. And to fast is better for you, if only you knew
phrases.ar: وَعَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُۥ فِدۡيَةٞ طَعَامُ مِسۡكِينٖۖ فَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرٗا فَهُوَ خَيۡرٞ لَّهُۥۚ وَأَن تَصُومُواْ خَيۡرٞ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The recitation is then discussed. The reading of all Muslims is and for those who are able to do it, and upon it their codices are based, and no one may deviate from it because of its transmission by all of them generation after generation, and Ibn Abbas used to read it as and for those who can manage it only with the utmost effort.

The reciters differed concerning its meaning. Some of them said that was at the beginning, when fasting was prescribed, and that whoever of the non-travellers was able to perform it would fast it if he wished, and if he wished he would break it and ransom it until that was abrogated. Others said that it was a special ruling for the man of great age and the old woman who were indeed able to fast, and that it was then abrogated, so that upon them rested fasting equal to what rested upon the young man.

The answer is then given. The men are excluded from being intended by it, for if the women alone were meant, it would have been said and for the women who are able to perform it, since that is how the Arabs speak when the statement is made specifically about them. And it is agreed by all that the resident healthy man who is able to fast is not permitted to break the fast and ransom it.

The meaning of the ransom is then given. It is the compensation, and the sense is that upon those who are able to perform the fasting there rests a compensation, the feeding of a needy person for each day that he breaks.

The recitation of the last clause is then discussed. Some read it with the ransom annexed to the food, and others with the two words separated, and the more correct is the annexation, since the ransom is the name of the action and is something other than the food with which the fasting is ransomed. And the reading of the needy person in the singular is preferred, because in clarifying the ruling of whoever breaks one day there lies access to the ruling of whoever breaks the whole month, and not the other way about.

The closing clause is then explained. And that you fast is better for you means that fasting what is prescribed for you of the month of Ramadan is better for you than that you break the fast and ransom it.

phrases.translation: Ramaḍân is the month in which the Quran was revealed as a guide for humanity with clear proofs of guidance and the standard ˹to distinguish between right and wrong˺.
phrases.ar: شَهۡرُ رَمَضَانَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ هُدٗى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتٖ مِّنَ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَٱلۡفُرۡقَانِۚ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ ٱلشَّهۡرَ فَلۡيَصُمۡهُۖ
phrases.explanation:
The month is explained first. The word for month is derived from the word for notoriety and making conspicuous, and one says of a man that he brandished his sword when he draws it from its sheath, and likewise the month became conspicuous when its new moon appears. As for Ramadan, some of the experts claimed that it was so named because of the intensity of the heat in it, to such a degree that the young camels were scorched by the hot ground.

The case of the word is then explained. It stands in the nominative in relation to the days mentioned earlier, and it is also permissible that the nominative carries the meaning that that is the month of Ramadan, and that the month has been prescribed for you. Some reciters have read it in the accusative with the meaning that fasting has been prescribed for you, namely that you fast the month of Ramadan, and it is also permissible to place it in the accusative as a command to fast it.

The two phrases are then explained. A guidance for mankind means a guide for mankind to the path of truth, and clear proofs means clear signs of guidance, that is to say the exposition that points to the limits of Allah and His obligations and what He has made permitted and forbidden.

A further point is then added. Others said that the meaning is that whoever among you witnesses the month, let him fast as much of it as he witnesses.

phrases.translation: So whoever is present this month, let them fast. But whoever is ill or on a journey, then ˹let them fast˺ an equal number of days ˹after Ramaḍân˺.
phrases.ar: وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٖ فَعِدَّةٞ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۗ
phrases.explanation:
The clause is explained first. Whoever is ill or on a journey during the month and on that account breaks the fast, upon him rests the fasting of the days that he broke, on days other than the days of Ramadan.

The people differed over the illness in which breaking the fast was permitted, and some said that it is the illness in which the affected person cannot perform his prayer standing.

The meaning of a number of other days is then given, and the grammar of the word for other is explained, since the days in the plural take feminine qualifications.

A question is then raised. If that is the interpretation, what of the man who was ill or on a journey and yet fasted the month? It is answered that the people of knowledge differed over all of this.

Some said that the breaking of the fast in illness is a binding obligation and not a concession, and those who held that said that whoever fasts on a journey must make it up when he becomes resident.

The indication of the verse is then given as sufficient. There is no greater hardship than that there should be imposed upon the man who fasted on his journey other days, and the saying that Allah desires for you ease is enough.

The reports about the messenger are then set out, that when he was asked about fasting on a journey he said, if you wish, fast, and if you wish, break the fast.

A question is then raised about the report that it is not of piety to fast on a journey, and it is answered that this applies only to a fasting in a condition such as that of the man to whom the report refers, and that whoever has had his fast broken to such a degree is not fasting out of piety.

phrases.translation: Allah intends ease for you, not hardship,
phrases.ar: يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡيُسۡرَ وَلَا
phrases.explanation:
The correct view is then given. The illness in which Allah has permitted the breaking of the fast is that of the man whom fasting exhausts in an unbearable manner, and for him there is the breaking of the fast and the making up of other days, since otherwise he would be burdened with hardship and the ease would be denied him. As for the man whom fasting does not exhaust, he has the status of the healthy person who can bear fasting.

A second statement is then given, and it is the most in accord with the correct view, since it is agreed by all that an ill person who fasts the month while he belongs to those for whom breaking is permitted has his fasting suffice him.

phrases.translation: so that you may complete the prescribed period and proclaim the greatness of Allah for guiding you, and perhaps you will be grateful
phrases.ar: يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡعُسۡرَ وَلِتُكۡمِلُواْ ٱلۡعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
phrases.explanation:
By and that you complete the number, the sense is that you complete the days that you broke, on other days imposed upon you to make up, after your recovery or your becoming resident.

The next clause is then explained. By and that you magnify Allah for that to which He has guided you, the sense is that you exalt Allah by the remembrance of Him on account of the guidance with which He has favoured you, which He withheld from others to whom the fasting of Ramadan had been prescribed.

The closing words are then explained. By and that you may perhaps be grateful, the sense is that you may thank Allah for that with which He has favoured you, and the word for perhaps here means that.

phrases.translation: When My servants ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about Me: I am truly near. I respond to one’s prayer when they call upon Me. So let them respond ˹with obedience˺ to Me and believe in Me, perhaps they will be guided ˹to the Right Way˺
phrases.ar: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌۖ أُجِيبُ دَعۡوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِۖ فَلۡيَسۡتَجِيبُواْ لِي وَلۡيُؤۡمِنُواْ بِي لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡشُدُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The question is explained first. By and when My servants ask you about Me, the sense is that they ask where I am, and indeed I am close to them, I hear their supplication and I answer the supplication of the one among them who supplicates.

The occasion of the revelation is then given. Some of them said that it was sent down because of a questioner who asked the prophet, saying, is our Lord near so that we may confide in Him, or is He far away so that we must call out to Him? Others said that it was sent down as an answer to the question of a group who asked the prophet, at what hour should we call upon Allah? And others said that it was sent down as an answer to the words of a group who, when Allah said to them, call upon Me and I will answer you, said, toward where should we call upon Him!

The clause about believing is then explained. And let them believe in Me means and let them affirm, so let them believe in Me when they respond to Me through obedience, that I stand as guarantor for them behind their obedience, regarding the reward for it and My generous bestowal of honour upon them.

The closing clause is then explained. That they may be rightly guided means so let them respond to Me through obedience and let them believe in Me, so that they affirm that upon their obedience there follows reward from Me, and let them thereby be guided to the right path.

The meaning of the supplication is then given at length. The first is that by the supplication is meant acting according to that which Allah has urged and commanded, so the sense is that I am near to the one who obeys Me and acts according to what I have commanded him, and I answer him with reward for his obedience, and the calling is the servant's request to his Lord for that which He has promised His faithful as reward, and the answering is the fulfilment of His promise. And it is related from the prophet in his saying, indeed the calling is the worship.

A second reading is then noted, that I answer the supplication of the supplicant when he calls upon Me, if I will it, so that it would be specific in meaning though phrased in general terms.

phrases.translation: It has been made permissible for you to be intimate with your wives during the nights preceding the fast. Your spouses are a garment for you as you are for them. Allah knows that you were deceiving yourselves. So He has accepted your repentance and pardoned you.
phrases.ar: أُحِلَّ لَكُمۡ لَيۡلَةَ ٱلصِّيَامِ ٱلرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَآئِكُمۡۚ هُنَّ لِبَاسٞ لَّكُمۡ وَأَنتُمۡ لِبَاسٞ لَّهُنَّۗ عَلِمَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّكُمۡ كُنتُمۡ تَخۡتَانُونَ أَنفُسَكُمۡ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَعَفَا عَنكُمۡۖ
phrases.explanation:
The opening is explained first. It has been made lawful for you means it has been released and permitted to you, and the night of the fast means on the night of the fast. And the word used is a euphemism for sexual intercourse, and it has been transmitted that in the recitation of Ibn Masud it reads with the plural form, and the people of interpretation have spoken in accordance with what has been said about the interpretation of it.

The metaphor of the garment is then examined at length. Your women are a garment for you and you are a garment for them, and the first possible meaning is that each of the two is made a garment for the other because of their being together during sleep, their coming together under one robe, and the joining of the body of each with that of the other, and a line of poetry is cited as a witness.

The other possibility is then given. Each of the two is made a garment for the other because he finds rest in the other, as He has made the night a garment and the wife a repose in which he finds rest.

A third sense is then added, that what covers a thing and conceals it from the eyes of onlookers is also said to be its garment and its covering, so it is possible that each of you is for the other a covering for what takes place between you of sexual intercourse.

phrases.translation: So now you may be intimate with them and seek what Allah has prescribed for you.
phrases.ar: فَٱلۡـَٰٔنَ بَٰشِرُوهُنَّ وَٱبۡتَغُواْ مَا كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۚ وَكُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ
phrases.explanation:
The word for intercourse is then explained. It is the coming together of skin with skin, and the skin of the man is his outer skin, and Allah has described by these words only sexual intercourse, so the sense is that now that He has made lawful for you intercourse with your women, then have intercourse with them in the nights of Ramadan until the dawn breaks, and that is the becoming distinct of the white thread from the black thread of the dawn.

The correct view is then given at length. By seek what Allah has prescribed for you, the sense is that you should seek what Allah the Exalted has decreed for you, and He means only that you should seek that which He has prescribed for you in the Preserved Tablet to be lawful, so that it is released to you. The seeking of the child, when the man seeks it by his intercourse with the woman, belongs to what has been prescribed for him, and likewise if he seeks what He has made lawful. All the meanings of the sought good may fall under the phrase, except that the meaning most consonant with the apparent form of the verse is that it means seek what Allah has prescribed for you of offspring, since it follows His saying, now have intercourse with them. So the sense that the phrase means seeking what Allah has prescribed in your intercourse with them of affection and progeny is more in accordance with the verse than the other interpretations, for which there is no indication of correctness in the apparent form of the revelation, nor a narration from the messenger.

phrases.translation: ˹You may˺ eat and drink until you see the light of dawn breaking the darkness of night, then complete the fast until nightfall. Do not be intimate with your spouses while you are meditating in the mosques. These are the limits set by Allah, so do not exceed them. This is how Allah makes His revelations clear to people, so they may become mindful ˹of Him˺
phrases.ar: حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡخَيۡطُ ٱلۡأَبۡيَضُ مِنَ ٱلۡخَيۡطِ ٱلۡأَسۡوَدِ مِنَ ٱلۡفَجۡرِۖ ثُمَّ أَتِمُّواْ ٱلصِّيَامَ إِلَى ٱلَّيۡلِۚ وَلَا تُبَٰشِرُوهُنَّ وَأَنتُمۡ عَٰكِفُونَ فِي ٱلۡمَسَٰجِدِۗ تِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَقۡرَبُوهَاۗ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَّقُونَ
phrases.explanation: The people of interpretation differed concerning this. Some said that by the white thread is meant the light of day, and by the black thread the darkness of night, and the interpretation according to that view is that you eat at night in the month of your fasting, and drink, and have intercourse with your women, seeking what Allah has prescribed for you of offspring, from the beginning of the night until the light of day appears to you through the breaking of the dawn out of the darkness of the night.

phrases.translation: Do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly, nor deliberately bribe authorities in order to devour a portion of others’ property, knowing that it is a sin
phrases.ar: وَلَا تَأۡكُلُوٓاْ أَمۡوَٰلَكُم بَيۡنَكُم بِٱلۡبَٰطِلِ وَتُدۡلُواْ بِهَآ إِلَى ٱلۡحُكَّامِ لِتَأۡكُلُواْ فَرِيقٗا مِّنۡ أَمۡوَٰلِ ٱلنَّاسِ بِٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَأَنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. Let not one of you consume the wealth of another through falsehood, and He made the one who consumes the wealth of his brother through falsehood equal to the one who consumes his own wealth through falsehood.

The second half is then explained. And do not litigate with your wealth before the judges, in order to consume a portion of the wealth of people through sin, while you know. And by through sin, the meaning is through the forbidden which Allah has declared forbidden to you, and while you know means that you deliberately consume that with premeditation regarding what Allah has declared forbidden, and in the knowledge that your deed is disobedience to Allah.

The word for lowering is then explained. Its origin is the letting down by a man of the bucket into a well, fastened to a rope, and it is said of the one who argues for his claim that he adduced such and such as argument, when his argument is a means for him to which he clings in his dispute, like the clinging of one who draws water from a well to a bucket which he has lowered into it. And the same is said of both adducing proof and lowering the bucket, with the same form of the verb.

phrases.translation: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about the phases of the moon. Say, “They are a means for people to determine time and pilgrimage.”
phrases.ar: يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡأَهِلَّةِۖ قُلۡ هِيَ مَوَٰقِيتُ لِلنَّاسِ وَٱلۡحَجِّۗ وَلَيۡسَ
phrases.explanation:
The occasion is then explained. It has been transmitted that the messenger was asked about the waxing and waning of the new moons and the variation in their states, whereupon Allah sent down this verse as an answer to that about which they asked.

The second half is then explained. By and the pilgrimage, the sense is that He also made them an appointed time for your pilgrimage, so that through them you may know the time of your rites and your pilgrimage.

phrases.translation: Righteousness is not in entering your houses from the back doors. Rather, righteousness is to be mindful ˹of Allah˺. So enter your homes through their ˹proper˺ doors,
phrases.ar: ٱلۡبِرُّ بِأَن تَأۡتُواْ ٱلۡبُيُوتَ مِن ظُهُورِهَا وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلۡبِرَّ مَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰۗ وَأۡتُواْ ٱلۡبُيُوتَ مِنۡ أَبۡوَٰبِهَاۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ
phrases.explanation:
It has been said that the verse was sent down concerning a people who, when they entered the state of ritual consecration, would not enter their houses through their doors.

The explanation of the verse is then given. Righteousness does not consist, O people, in your entering the houses in the state of your consecration from their backs, but righteous is he who fears Allah, so fears Him and avoids His prohibitions, and obeys Him by performing His obligations. And as for entering the houses from their backs, in that there is no righteousness toward Allah. So enter them from whichever side you wish, through their doors or otherwise, so long as you do not believe that it is forbidden to enter them through their doors in any state, for that is not permissible for you to believe.

phrases.translation: and be mindful of Allah so you may be successful
phrases.ar: ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
phrases.explanation: The closing words are then explained. And fear Allah, O people, so be on your guard against Him and hold Him in awe by obeying Him in what He has imposed upon you of His obligations, and by avoiding what He has forbidden you, so that you may succeed and thereby attain your desires with Him, and thereby reach the abiding in His gardens and the eternity in His bliss. And the meaning of success was expounded earlier with that which indicates it.

phrases.translation: Fight in the cause of Allah ˹only˺ against those who wage war against you, but do not exceed the limits. Allah does not like transgressors
phrases.ar: وَقَٰتِلُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُقَٰتِلُونَكُمۡ وَلَا تَعۡتَدُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُعۡتَدِينَ
phrases.explanation:
The question of abrogation is discussed first, and the correct view is given. It is the statement that Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz made, since the claim of a verse being abrogated while it is possible that it is not, without proof for the correctness of the claim, is arbitrariness.

The explanation of the verse is then given. And fight, O believers, in the way of Allah, and His way is the path He has made clear and the religion He has prescribed for His servants, so fight in obedience to Me and according to what I have prescribed for you of My religion, and call to that whoever has turned away from it, with the hands and the tongues, until they return to obedience to Me, or they give you the jizyah in humility if they are people of the book. And He commanded them to fight those from whom fighting issued among the combatants of the people of disbelief.

The last clause is then explained. Do not kill a newborn, nor a woman, nor whoever gives you the jizyah, and those who overstep His limits are the transgressors.

phrases.translation: Kill them wherever you come upon them and drive them out of the places from which they have driven you out.
phrases.ar: وَٱقۡتُلُوهُمۡ حَيۡثُ ثَقِفۡتُمُوهُمۡ وَأَخۡرِجُوهُم مِّنۡ حَيۡثُ أَخۡرَجُوكُمۡۚ
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. Kill, O believers, those among the polytheists who wage war against you, wherever you encounter them in a condition in which you are able to overcome them and kill them.

The word is then explained. Its meaning with regard to a matter is to be skilled and sharp-sighted in it, and one says of a man that he is truly on his guard in battle when he has keen perception of the places where killing can be done, and the word has another meaning, namely the straightening. So kill them in every place where you are able to kill them and where you have keen perception of the places where they can be killed.

phrases.translation: For persecution is far worse than killing.
phrases.ar: وَٱلۡفِتۡنَةُ أَشَدُّ مِنَ ٱلۡقَتۡلِۚ
phrases.explanation:
The clause is then explained. And the tribulation is worse than killing means that ascribing partners to Allah is worse than killing.

The meaning of it is then set out. The trial of the believer in his religion, until he apostatises from it and thus, after his Islam, becomes one who ascribes partners to Allah, is worse for him and more harmful than that he be killed while remaining steadfast in his religion, holding fast to it and adhering to the truth in it.

phrases.translation: And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque unless they attack you there. If they do so, then fight them—that is the reward of the disbelievers
phrases.ar: وَلَا تُقَٰتِلُوهُمۡ عِندَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ حَتَّىٰ يُقَٰتِلُوكُمۡ فِيهِۖ فَإِن قَٰتَلُوكُمۡ فَٱقۡتُلُوهُمۡۗ كَذَٰلِكَ جَزَآءُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. And do not fight them at the sacred mosque until they fight you there, but if they fight you, then kill them, such is the recompense of the unbelievers.

The recitation is then discussed. The reciters of Medina and Mecca read it as do not fight them at the sacred mosque until they fight you there, so that you do not begin the fighting against the polytheists there until they begin it against you, but if they begin against you in the sacred precinct then kill them, since Allah has set as recompense for the unbelievers being killed in this life and prolonged humiliation in the hereafter. And most of the reciters of Kufa read it as do not kill them until they kill you there.

The correct reading is then given. It is the first, because Allah did not command His prophet and his companions to surrender themselves to the polytheists until they had first made one slain among themselves, after the fighting had already been permitted, so that the reading containing the permission to kill them only after they have killed one of them has no preference over it. And it is known that He had already permitted them to fight when the beginning of the fighting came from the polytheists, both before they had killed anyone of them and after.

phrases.translation: But if they cease, then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.ar: فَإِنِ ٱنتَهَوۡاْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٞ رَّحِيمٞ
phrases.explanation: The clause is then explained. If the unbelievers whom you fight cease from fighting you and from their unbelief in Allah, and they desist from that and repent, then Allah is indeed forgiving with regard to the sins of whoever among them believes and repents from his polytheism and returns to Allah from his acts of disobedience and the days that have passed, and merciful toward him in his hereafter through His favour to him and by granting him what He grants to the people of obedience of reward, on account of his return to what He loves from his disobedience.

phrases.translation: Fight against them ˹if they persecute you˺ until there is no more persecution,
phrases.ar: وَقَٰتِلُوهُمۡ حَتَّىٰ لَا تَكُونَ فِتۡنَةٞ وَيَكُونَ
phrases.explanation: The command is explained first. And fight the polytheists who fight you until there is no more trial, meaning until there is no more ascribing of partners to Allah, and until none is worshipped besides Him, and the worship of idols, gods and equals ceases, and worship and obedience belong to Allah alone to the exclusion of the other false deities and idols, as Qatada said.

phrases.translation: and ˹your˺ devotion will be to Allah ˹alone˺.
phrases.ar: ٱلدِّينُ لِلَّهِۖ
phrases.explanation: The words are then explained. When they abhorred the religion, he means when they abhorred obedience and refused it. And his word that he humbled them means he humbled them, subdued them and compelled them to obedience. And his word successive means the one overtaking the other, and the assault is the assault, and to assault against his enemy means he leapt upon him and attacked him. He says, he continued his raids and assaults relentlessly until they submitted in obedience.

phrases.translation: If they stop ˹persecuting you˺, let there be no hostility except against the aggressors
phrases.ar: فَإِنِ ٱنتَهَوۡاْ فَلَا عُدۡوَٰنَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
phrases.explanation:
The clause is explained first. But if the unbelievers who fight you cease fighting you, and they enter your community of faith, and they acknowledge what Allah has imposed upon you as obligations, and they abandon that which they were upon, namely the worship of idols, then abandon the hostility against them, the fighting of them and the struggle against them. For it is not fitting that hostility be committed except against the wrongdoers, and they are those who ascribe partners to Allah and those who have abandoned His worship and worship another than their Creator.

This is entirely comparable to His saying that Allah mocks them, and to the saying that they ridicule them and Allah ridicules them, and the explanation of this and of similar cases was set forth earlier.

phrases.translation: ˹There will be retaliation in˺ a sacred month for ˹an offence in˺ a sacred month, and all violations will bring about retaliation. So, if anyone attacks you, retaliate in the same manner.
phrases.ar: ٱلشَّهۡرُ ٱلۡحَرَامُ بِٱلشَّهۡرِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ وَٱلۡحُرُمَٰتُ قِصَاصٞۚ فَمَنِ ٱعۡتَدَىٰ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فَٱعۡتَدُواْ عَلَيۡهِ بِمِثۡلِ مَا ٱعۡتَدَىٰ عَلَيۡكُمۡۚ
phrases.explanation:
The sacred month is explained first. By the sacred month for the sacred month, the sense is the month of Dhu al-Qada, in which the messenger intended to perform the lesser pilgrimage of al-Hudaybiya, and in which the polytheists of Mecca barred him from access to the sacred house. He made peace that year on the condition that he would return the following year, enter Mecca and remain there three days. When the following year came he set out with his companions, and the inhabitants vacated the city for him, and he completed his lesser pilgrimage and returned to Medina. Then Allah said to His prophet and the Muslims with him, the sacred month, that is Dhu al-Qada, in which Allah brought you to His sanctuary despite the aversion of the polytheists, for the sacred month, in which they had barred you the preceding year, so Allah granted you retaliation against them in that He caused you to enter the sanctuary despite their aversion, in exchange for what they had done to you.

The name of the month is then explained. Allah called it the sacred month only because the Arabs in the time of ignorance held fighting and killing to be forbidden therein and laid down their weapons, and they had named it Dhu al-Qada because of their sitting therein, abstaining from raids and wars, so Allah named it by the name with which the Arabs used to name it.

The more fitting of the two interpretations is then given, that which is transmitted from Mujahid, since the verses before it are nothing other than a command to fight in a particular manner, and the sentence about aggression stands only in the context of the command to fighting, and Allah did not prescribe fighting for the believers except after the migration.

From this it is known that the sentence is Medinan and not Meccan, and that it is equal to the saying, fight those who fight you, so whoever commits aggression against you in the sanctuary then commit aggression against him by means of fighting, proportionate to his aggression against you, for I have made the sacred things a matter of retaliation. And the other interpretation is then given, that the word means the rushing and pouncing, so whoever rushes upon you with wrongdoing then rush upon him as retaliation and not out of wrongdoing.

phrases.translation: ˹But˺ be mindful of Allah, and know that Allah is with those mindful ˹of Him˺
phrases.ar: وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
phrases.explanation: The closing words are then explained. And fear Allah, O believers, with regard to His sacred things and His limits, that you commit no transgression therein and do not overstep therein what He has set forth and bounded for you. And know that Allah loves the God-fearing, who fear Him by fulfilling His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions.

phrases.translation: Spend in the cause of Allah
phrases.ar: وَأَنفِقُواْ فِي
phrases.explanation:
The meanings are discussed first. Some of them said that what is meant is that the way of Allah is His path along which He has commanded marching out against His enemy among the polytheists, and that do not cast yourselves into destruction means do not abandon spending in the way of Allah, for Allah will recompense you for it with a reward and will soon provide for you in this life. Others said that the meaning is that spending is intended, and that do not cast yourselves into destruction means do not march out in the way of Allah without provisions and without the means to bear it. Others said that it means through the sins you have committed, so that you despair of the mercy of Allah, but hope for His mercy and perform good deeds.

The correct view is then given. Allah commanded spending in His way, and His way is the path He has prescribed for His servants and made clear to them, so the meaning is that you spend in making strong His religion through struggle against your enemy who has set up war against you on account of disbelief in Him, and He forbade them to cast themselves into destruction with their own hands.

And since all these meanings can be borne by the words, and Allah has not singled out any of them above another, the correct view is that Allah has forbidden us to cast ourselves down with our own hands into that in which our ruin lies, and to surrender ourselves to ruin, namely the punishment, by abandoning the obligations He has imposed upon us. It is therefore not permitted for us to engage in anything Allah disapproves of, that by which we deserve His punishment.

phrases.translation: and do not let your own hands throw you into destruction ˹by withholding˺.
phrases.ar: سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا تُلۡقُواْ بِأَيۡدِيكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلتَّهۡلُكَةِ
phrases.explanation:
A question is raised about the reason for the insertion of the particle in the words and do not cast yourselves with your own hands, since it is customary in well-known usage to say I threw so-and-so a dirham and not with a dirham.

The answer is then given. It has been said that it is added, just as the speaker adds the particle in his words I pulled at the garment and I pulled the garment, and I clung to it and I clung it, and in the saying of the one who brings forth oil, while it is in fact brings forth the oil.

phrases.translation: And do good, for Allah certainly loves the good-doers
phrases.ar: وَأَحۡسِنُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
phrases.explanation: The closing words are then explained. By and do good, the sense is do good, O believers, in fulfilling the obligations that I have imposed upon you, in avoiding what I have commanded you to avoid of acts of disobedience to Me, in spending in My way, and in the returning of the strong among you to the weak who is in need, for I love those who do good in that.

phrases.translation: Complete the pilgrimage and minor pilgrimage for Allah. But if prevented ˹from proceeding˺, then ˹offer˺ whatever sacrificial animals you can afford. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal reaches its destination. But if any of you is ill or has a scalp ailment ˹requiring shaving˺,
phrases.ar: وَأَتِمُّواْ ٱلۡحَجَّ وَٱلۡعُمۡرَةَ لِلَّهِۚ فَإِنۡ أُحۡصِرۡتُمۡ فَمَا ٱسۡتَيۡسَرَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَدۡيِۖ وَلَا تَحۡلِقُواْ رُءُوسَكُمۡ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡلُغَ ٱلۡهَدۡيُ مَحِلَّهُۥۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ بِهِۦٓ أَذٗى مِّن رَّأۡسِهِۦ فَفِدۡيَةٞ مِّن صِيَامٍ
phrases.explanation:
The scholars differed concerning the prevention for which Allah imposed upon the one afflicted by it the duty of whatever is easy of a sacrificial animal. Some of them said that it is every impediment or detainer that impeded the person in the state of consecration.

The more correct interpretation is then given. If the fear of an enemy, or an illness, or an affliction prevents you from coming to the house, that is to say, your fear or your illness causes you to hold yourselves back, and therefore it was said if you are prevented, because the mention of the fear and the illness has been omitted.

The occasion of the verse is then given. It was sent down on the occasion of the lesser pilgrimage of al-Hudaybiya, at which one was prevented.

phrases.translation: then compensate either by fasting, charity, or a sacrificial offering.
phrases.ar: أَوۡ صَدَقَةٍ أَوۡ نُسُكٖۚ فَإِذَآ
phrases.explanation:
The question is then raised. If those who refused that the sheep falls under whatever is easy of a sacrificial animal held that it does not deserve the name of sacrificial animal, any more than if someone were to offer a chicken or an egg, then it is said that if there were a disagreement about the chicken and the egg like that about the sheep, their way would be the same.

But since that which is less than the yearling of the sheep and the two-year-old of the goats is excluded from being a valid sacrificial animal, by the proof transmitted from the prophet, that was excluded from being intended.

phrases.translation: In times of peace, you may combine the pilgrimage and minor pilgrimage then make the sacrificial offering you can afford. Whoever cannot afford that ˹offering˺, let them fast three days during pilgrimage and seven after returning ˹home˺—completing ten. These offerings are for those who do not live near the Sacred House. And be mindful of Allah, and know that Allah is severe in punishment
phrases.ar: أَمِنتُمۡ فَمَن تَمَتَّعَ بِٱلۡعُمۡرَةِ إِلَى ٱلۡحَجِّ فَمَا ٱسۡتَيۡسَرَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَدۡيِۚ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامٖ فِي ٱلۡحَجِّ وَسَبۡعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعۡتُمۡۗ تِلۡكَ عَشَرَةٞ كَامِلَةٞۗ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن لَّمۡ يَكُنۡ أَهۡلُهُۥ حَاضِرِي ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
phrases.explanation: The scholars then differed again concerning the meaning of whatever is easy of a sacrificial animal. Some of them said that it is a sheep, and the report naming who said that is given. And others said that it is something from the camels and the cattle, but of a younger age than the regular age, and the report naming who said that is given.

phrases.translation: ˹Commitment to˺ pilgrimage is made in appointed months.
phrases.ar: ٱلۡحَجُّ أَشۡهُرٞ مَّعۡلُومَٰتٞۚ فَمَن
phrases.explanation:
The months are explained first. The pilgrimage takes place in well-known months, meaning that the time of the pilgrimage is the well-known months.
