The months stand in the nominative because of the pilgrimage, even though the pilgrimage forms a temporal determination for them and not an adjectival qualification, because they are not delimited by a definition through annexation to a specific concept, and the same is the case in the expression of the Arabs, the Muslims on one side and the unbelievers on the other side.

A question is then raised about the basis of those who say the pilgrimage occupies three full months, when the rites of the pilgrimage are not performed after the passing of the days of Mina. It is answered that by their statement they meant that the pilgrimage occupies three full months only in the sense that they are the months of the pilgrimage and not the months of the lesser pilgrimage, even though the rites of the pilgrimage are performed only in a part of them.

A further question is then raised, how the pilgrimage can be said to be months when it is two months and a part of the third. It is answered that the Arabs do not refrain, particularly with regard to temporal designations, from the use of something of the like, since one says I have not seen him for two days while one means thereby only one day and a part of another, and one may perform an act in a single hour and then ascribe it to the whole year.

The undertaking of the pilgrimage is then explained. Whoever makes the pilgrimage obligatory upon himself and binds himself to it in these months, and making it obligatory upon oneself is the firm resolve to perform everything that Allah has imposed upon the pilgrim and to abstain from everything He has commanded him to abstain from.

The three possibilities are then set out. The undertaking may consist of the firm resolve alone, or of the firm resolve together with the proclamation of the pilgrimage, or of the firm resolve with the man in the state of consecration through imposing it upon himself, even though that is not manifested by the divesting of clothing and the proclamation and the performance of a part of the rites. And since the first two possibilities are invalid, the third is the correct one, so the undertaking of the pilgrimage is that whose obligation is connected with the firm resolve.

phrases.translation: Whoever commits to ˹performing˺ pilgrimage, let them stay away from intimate relations, foul language, and arguments during pilgrimage. Whatever good you do, Allah ˹fully˺ knows of it. Take ˹necessary˺ provisions ˹for the journey˺—surely the best provision is righteousness. And be mindful of Me, O people of reason
phrases.ar: فَرَضَ فِيهِنَّ ٱلۡحَجَّ فَلَا رَفَثَ وَلَا فُسُوقَ وَلَا جِدَالَ فِي ٱلۡحَجِّۗ وَمَا تَفۡعَلُواْ مِنۡ خَيۡرٖ يَعۡلَمۡهُ ٱللَّهُۗ وَتَزَوَّدُواْ فَإِنَّ خَيۡرَ ٱلزَّادِ ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰۖ وَٱتَّقُونِ يَٰٓأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
phrases.explanation:
The exegetes differed concerning the meaning by which a man undertakes the pilgrimage, after the agreement of all of them that the meaning of undertaking is obligation and binding. Some of them said that the undertaking of the pilgrimage is the pronouncing of the proclamation, and the report naming who said that is given.

They differed again concerning the meaning of the word for obscenity in this place. Some of them said that it is the uttering of obscenities to the woman in words, namely that he says, when we are out of the state of consecration, I will do this and that with you, without veiling it, and the report naming who said that is given.

They differed again concerning the meaning of the word for transgression. Some of them said that it is all acts of disobedience, and the report naming who said that is given. And others said that it is that by which one disobeys Allah during the consecration of what He has forbidden therein, such as the killing of game, the removal of hair and the cutting of nails, and the like.

phrases.translation: There is no blame on you for seeking the bounty of your Lord ˹during this journey˺.
phrases.ar: لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَبۡتَغُواْ فَضۡلٗا مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡۚ
phrases.explanation:
The permission is explained first. There is no blame on you that you seek a bounty from your Lord.

It has been said that the meaning of seeking the bounty of Allah is seeking Allah's provision by means of trade, and that this verse was revealed concerning a people who held the view that one was not permitted to engage in trade when one had entered the state of ritual consecration, thereby seeking piety. Then He let them know that there was no piety in that, and that it was permitted for them to seek His bounty by means of selling and buying.

phrases.translation: When you return from ’Arafât,
phrases.ar: فَإِذَآ أَفَضۡتُم مِّنۡ عَرَفَٰتٖ
phrases.explanation:
The reason for the name is then discussed. The scholars differed concerning why Arafat is called Arafat. Some of them said that it was so named because Abraham, the bosom friend of Allah, recognized it when he saw it, by the description of it that he had with him, and said, I have recognized it, after which it was called Arafat for that reason. And that saying indicates that it is a name for the place and that it was so named after itself and what lies around it, as one says a worn-out garment and a flat land, where the singular is put in the plural on account of what lies around it.

The correct view is then given. It is a name for a single place, named with a plural, so if it is declined with nunation it is taken in the sense of the plural that it originally was, and if the nunation is omitted it is taken as the name of a single known place, and then the nunation is omitted just as it is omitted in the names of known towns and villages.

phrases.translation: praise Allah near the sacred place
phrases.ar: فَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عِندَ ٱلۡمَشۡعَرِ
phrases.explanation:
The remembrance is then explained. When you depart and return from Arafat to the place from which you had begun the journey toward it, then remember Allah, and this means the prayer and the supplication at the sacred standing place.

A point of grammar is then added. The landmarks have already been explained as derived from the saying of a person, I knew it, and the landmark is so named because the prayer at it, the abiding, the spending of the night and the supplication belong to the landmarks and obligations of the pilgrimage.

The saying of Abdullah ibn Umar is then explained. When he came to al-Muzdalifa he said, all of this are landmarks up to Mecca, and the meaning of that is that they are landmarks among the landmarks of the pilgrimage, at which one performs in each place a portion of the rites, and not that all of that is the sacred standing place, such that whoever halts wherever he halts of it up to the interior of Mecca would thereby have fulfilled what is imposed upon him.

phrases.translation: and praise Him for having guided you, for surely before this ˹guidance˺ you were astray
phrases.ar: ٱلۡحَرَامِۖ وَٱذۡكُرُوهُ كَمَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَإِن كُنتُم مِّن قَبۡلِهِۦ لَمِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
phrases.explanation:
The clause is explained first. And remember Him as He has guided you, and the sense is that you remember Allah at the sacred standing place by praising Him and thanking Him for His favours upon you, and let your remembrance of Him be through submission to His command, obedience to Him and gratitude for the grace with which He has favoured you regarding the success toward the practices of Abraham after the state of ascribing partners, bewilderment and blindness regarding the way of truth, and after the going astray, just as His remembrance of you through guidance rescued you from the fire after you stood at the edge of a precipice of it, and that is the meaning of as He has guided you.

The last clause is then addressed. Among the linguists there are those who direct the interpretation of the word in toward the meaning of negation and the interpretation of the particle toward except, and the meaning of that is that you remember Allah as He has remembered you with guidance and thus guided you toward that which was pleasing to Him of the religions, while you were already before that time among those who went astray.

phrases.translation: Then go forth with the rest of the pilgrims. And seek Allah’s forgiveness.
phrases.ar: ثُمَّ أَفِيضُواْ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ أَفَاضَ ٱلنَّاسُ
phrases.explanation:
The exegetes differed over the explanation of this. Who is meant by the command to pour forth from where the people pour forth, and who are the people who were commanded to pour forth from there?

One answer is then given. What is meant by then pour forth are the Quraysh and those whom the Quraysh had begotten, who in the time of ignorance were called the Hums, and in Islam they were commanded to pour forth from Arafat, which is the place from which all the remaining people poured forth, because the Quraysh said, we do not leave the sacred precinct, and so they were not present at the standing place at Arafa together with them.

Another answer is given, that those addressed are all the Muslims together, and that from where the people pour forth means from Jam, and that by the people is meant Abraham.

The correct view is then given. By this verse the Quraysh are meant, and those among the remaining Arabs who had joined themselves to the Hums, on account of the agreement among the exegetes.

The explanation of the verse is then given as a whole, that whoever undertakes the pilgrimage as an obligation has no sexual intercourse nor licentious conduct nor dispute during it, then pours forth from where the people pour forth and asks Allah for forgiveness.

A further point is then made. Were it not for the agreement that has been described, the correct of the two explanations would be that of al-Dahhak, namely that from where the people pour forth means from where Abraham poured forth, since the pouring forth from Arafat is undoubtedly before that from Jam. And the answer is given, that the Arabs do that frequently, since they indicate the singular by the mention of the plural.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.ar: وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرُواْ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٞ رَّحِيمٞ
phrases.explanation: The closing words are then explained. When you then pour forth from Arafat, on the way to Mina, then remember Allah at the sacred standing place, and call upon Him and worship Him there, just as He has guided you with His guidance and favoured you with that with which He pleased His friend Abraham, to which He guided him of the prescriptions of His religion, after you had strayed from it.

phrases.translation: When you have fulfilled your sacred rites, praise Allah as you used to praise your forefathers ˹before Islam˺, or even more passionately. There are some who say, “Our Lord! Grant us ˹Your bounties˺ in this world,” but they will have no share in the Hereafter
phrases.ar: فَإِذَا قَضَيۡتُم مَّنَٰسِكَكُمۡ فَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ كَذِكۡرِكُمۡ ءَابَآءَكُمۡ أَوۡ أَشَدَّ ذِكۡرٗاۗ فَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَمَا لَهُۥ فِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ مِنۡ خَلَٰقٖ
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. When you have completed your rites, meaning when you have finished your pilgrimage and have slaughtered your sacrificial animals, then remember Allah.

Two explanations are then given. Some of them said that the people in the time of ignorance used to gather after finishing their pilgrimage and boast about the glorious deeds of their fathers, and then Allah commanded them in Islam that their remembrance should consist of praise, gratitude and glorification of their Lord and no one else, and that they should obligate themselves to remember Him abundantly, after the example of the remembrance of their fathers. Others said that it was said to them, remember Allah as you remember your fathers, because they, when they had completed their rites and called upon their Lord, remembered no one but their fathers, and then they were commanded to remember Allah in a manner corresponding to their remembrance of their fathers.

The correct statement is then given. Allah commanded His believing servants to remember Him through obedience to Him, in submission to His command and worship of Him, after the completion of their rites, and this remembrance may be the proclamation of the greatness of Allah which He commanded with His saying, and remember Allah during a numbered number of days, for He obligated him at that moment to a remembrance of Him that had not previously been obligatory for him, and urged perseverance in it, just as the sons persevere in remembering the fathers in their transmitted deeds, by submitting to Him and turning humbly to Him in their yearning for Him in their needs, as the child turns humbly to his father, or even stronger than that, since every favor that befell them and their fathers comes from Him.

The second half of the verse is then explained. Remember Allah as you remember your fathers, or with even stronger remembrance, and turn yearningly to Him for the good of this world and the hereafter that is with Him, with supplication and humility, and make your deeds pure for the sake of His face, and do not be like the one who has bought the worldly life at the expense of the hereafter, so that there is for them no portion in the reward of Allah nor any share in His gardens and in the noble things He has prepared for His protégés.

The meaning of share is then noted, that it means the portion, and it was explained elsewhere with the testimonies from the proofs.

phrases.translation: Yet there are others who say, “Our Lord! Grant us the good of this world and the Hereafter, and protect us from the torment of the Fire.”
phrases.ar: وَمِنۡهُم مَّن يَقُولُ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا حَسَنَةٗ وَفِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ حَسَنَةٗ وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ
phrases.explanation:
The people described are explained first. The correct view concerning that is that Allah has informed about a group of people who believe in Him and in His messenger, among them those who have performed the pilgrimage to His House, that they ask their Lord for the good in this world and the good in the hereafter, and that He protect them from the punishment of the fire. And the good from Allah may comprise well-being in the body, livelihood, provision and the like, as well as knowledge and worship.

Two other readings are then recorded. Some of them said that what is meant is that among the people are those who say, our Lord, give us well-being in this world and well-being in the hereafter. And others said that Allah intended by the good, in this world, knowledge and worship, and in the hereafter, the garden.

The closing clause is then explained. And protect us from the punishment of the fire means turn away from us the punishment of the fire.

phrases.translation: It is they who will receive a ˹heavenly˺ reward for the good they have done. Surely Allah is swift in reckoning
phrases.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمۡ نَصِيبٞ مِّمَّا كَسَبُواْۚ وَٱللَّهُ سَرِيعُ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
phrases.explanation:
The people meant are then explained. By those, He means those who, after the completion of their pilgrimage rites, say, our Lord, give us in this world good and in the hereafter good and protect us from the punishment of the fire, out of their longing toward Allah for what is with Him. Thus He has made known that they have a portion and a share in their pilgrimage and an abundant reward for the work they have earned.

The closing words are then explained. And Allah is swift in the reckoning means that He encompasses the work of both groups, that of the one whose request is give us in this world, and that of the other whose request is give us in this world good and in the hereafter good, and then He recompenses each for its work.

phrases.translation: And remember Allah during ˹these˺ appointed days.
phrases.ar: وَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ فِيٓ أَيَّامٖ مَّعۡدُودَٰتٖۚ فَمَن
phrases.explanation:
The days are explained first. Remember Allah by professing His oneness and by proclaiming His greatness during a counted number of days, and these are the days of casting the pebbles, for He commanded His servants on those days to perform the proclamation of the greatness after the prayers and at the casting, with each pebble of the pebbles with which one pelts one of the pillars.

A question is then raised. When the prophet said concerning the days of Mina that they are days of eating and drinking and the remembrance of Allah, he did not inform his community that these are the appointed days which Allah mentions in His Book, so what then do you deny in the possibility that the prophet intended by the remembrance of Allah the well-known days.

phrases.translation: Whoever departs swiftly on the second day is not sinful, neither are those who stay behind ˹till the third—seeking additional reward˺, so long as they are mindful ˹of their Lord˺.
phrases.ar: تَعَجَّلَ فِي يَوۡمَيۡنِ فَلَآ إِثۡمَ عَلَيۡهِ وَمَن تَأَخَّرَ فَلَآ إِثۡمَ عَلَيۡهِۖ لِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰۗ وَٱتَّقُواْ
phrases.explanation:
The sentence is explained first. Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him, for whoever fears.

The exegetes differed concerning its meaning. Some of them said that whoever hastens in two of the days of tashriq and departs on the second day has no sin upon him in his departing, and whoever delays his departure until the third day has no sin upon him in his delaying. Others said that the meaning is that there is no objection upon him in his hastening his departure, if he is careful not to kill game until the third day has passed, and whoever delays until the third day and does not depart earlier, there is no objection upon him. Others said that the sense is that he is forgiven, if he is careful not to strike anything in his pilgrimage that Allah has forbidden him.

The meaning preferred is then given at length. Similar narrations indicate that whoever performs the pilgrimage and accomplishes it according to its limits as Allah has commanded him comes out of his sins, for there lay in the words of the messenger that which clarifies that the meaning of the sentence is that he comes out of his sins, that his sins have been taken away from him and his offenses forgiven him. And the objection is removed from the agent only with respect to something whose omission rested upon him, so that it is permitted to him to do it, or with respect to something whose doing rested upon him, so that it is permitted to him to omit it. As for that whose doing rests upon the agent, there is no sense in removing the objection from him if he does it, while his duty is precisely the doing of it.

And since the pilgrim can be in no other case than that his duty is departure on the second day, or that his duty is remaining until the third day, it follows that if his duty on the second day is remaining until the third, then the second clause has no meaning.

The narration of the messenger explicitly declares that he, by accomplishing his pilgrimage as he was commanded, comes out of his sins as on the day his mother bore him, and therein lies a clear indication of the incorrectness of the view that the meaning is that there is no sin upon him from the moment of completing the pilgrimage until the following year.

The answer to that is then given. What governs it is the meaning of the sentence, for in it lies the meaning that the sins have been taken away and the offenses remitted, so the mention of the remission of sins was omitted because the indication of the sentence sufficed.

A grammatical point is then added. Some of the grammarians of Basra have claimed that it is as though He thereby informed of something, and so said, for whoever fears, that is to say, this is for whoever fears. And another possibility is then given, namely that neither of the two groups is to brand the other as sinful.

phrases.translation: And be mindful of Allah, and know that to Him you will ˹all˺ be gathered
phrases.ar: ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّكُمۡ إِلَيۡهِ تُحۡشَرُونَ
phrases.explanation: The closing words are then explained. And fear Allah, O believers, in that which He has imposed upon you of obligations, fear Him against neglecting and failing in them, and in that which He has forbidden you in your pilgrimage and your rites, and in that with which He has charged you in your consecration, that you should fall short in accomplishing and carrying it out. And know that to Him you will be gathered, for He will requite you according to your deeds, and repay every soul among you in full for what it has performed, while no injustice will be done to you.

phrases.translation: There are some ˹hypocrites˺ who impress you with their views regarding worldly affairs and openly call upon Allah to witness what is in their hearts, yet they are your worst adversaries
phrases.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُعۡجِبُكَ قَوۡلُهُۥ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَيُشۡهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِي قَلۡبِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَلَدُّ ٱلۡخِصَامِ
phrases.explanation:
The description is explained first. This is a description by Allah of the hypocrites, that among the people is one whose outward speech and open declaration please you, and who calls Allah to witness over what is in his heart, while he is the most contentious of disputants, a disputant by means of falsehood.

The occasion of the revelation is then discussed. Some of them said that it was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, who came to the messenger and claimed that he desired Islam and swore that he had come only for that, and then went off and wrought harm among the possessions of the Muslims. Others said that it was revealed about a group of the people of hypocrisy who spoke about the raiding party of the messenger that was struck down at al-Raji. And others said that by it were meant all the hypocrites, and by the phrase about the contradiction between their inner and their outer.

The recitation is then discussed. There are two modes of reading the clause about calling Allah to witness. Most of the readers read it as he calls Allah to witness over what is in his heart, with the meaning that the hypocrite whose speech pleases the messenger calls Allah to witness over what is in his heart, that his speech accords with his conviction and that he believes in Allah and His messenger, while he is lying.

A report from Allah is then given, that the hypocrite about whom He informed His prophet that he pleases him when his word and his speech please him calls Allah to witness that he speaks the truth in that saying of his, on account of the severity of his dispute and his contentiousness by means of falsehood and the lie of speech.

phrases.translation: And when they leave ˹you˺, they strive throughout the land to spread mischief in it and destroy crops and cattle. Allah does not like mischief
phrases.ar: وَإِذَا تَوَلَّىٰ سَعَىٰ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ لِيُفۡسِدَ فِيهَا وَيُهۡلِكَ ٱلۡحَرۡثَ وَٱلنَّسۡلَۚ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡفَسَادَ
phrases.explanation:
The correct view is then given. Allah described this hypocrite as one who, when he turns away and turns his back on the messenger, commits corruption upon the earth of Allah, and under the phrase of spreading corruption all forms of disobedience may fall, since committing disobedience is corruption upon the earth, so Allah did not restrict His description to some meanings of it to the exclusion of others. Except that what most resembles the apparent meaning is that he cut off the road and spread fear upon the path.

The manner of the destroying is then discussed. The exegetes differed concerning it, and his destroying of the seed sown is his burning of it. And it may be that it was as Mujahid said, through the withholding of the rain on account of his disobedience, and it may be that it was through his killing of those who tend it until it spoiled, and likewise the destroying of the offspring was through his killing of the mothers or the fathers, so that in his killing of them lies the cutting off of their offspring. And what is more in agreement with the apparent meaning is what al-Suddi said, except that al-Suddi mentioned that this verse was revealed only about his killing of the donkeys of the group of Muslims and his burning of a crop of theirs, and although it is permissible that it was so, it is not incorrect that the verse was revealed about him while what is meant by it is anyone who walks his path in killing all that he killed of animals whose killing is not permitted under any circumstance. For Allah did not single out any of that above anything else, but He made it general.

A recitation is then noted, that some reciters have read the words with the nominative, and the meaning given is that and the crops and the offspring perish.

The closing clause is then explained, that Allah does not love the deeds of disobedience, and the cutting off of the path and the spreading of fear upon the road. And a point of grammar is added, that the word for corruption is a verbal noun from the saying of a person that the thing became corrupt, it becomes corrupt, comparable to their saying of going, he goes, a going.

phrases.translation: When it is said to them, “Fear Allah,” pride carries them off to sin. Hell will be their proper place. What an evil place to rest
phrases.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُ ٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ أَخَذَتۡهُ ٱلۡعِزَّةُ بِٱلۡإِثۡمِۚ فَحَسۡبُهُۥ جَهَنَّمُۖ وَلَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمِهَادُ
phrases.explanation:
The verse is explained first. He means that when it is said to this hypocrite, whose characteristic He described to His prophet, fear Allah and be wary of Him, then arrogance seizes him in sin.

The people of interpretation differed concerning whom this verse means. Some of them said that by it was meant every transgressor and hypocrite, and the report naming who said that is given. And others said that by it was meant al-Akhnas ibn Shariq.

The closing words are then explained. And what a wretched resting place means what a wretched sleeping place and bed is hell, which he has prepared for himself through his hypocrisy.

phrases.translation: And there are those who would dedicate their lives to Allah’s pleasure.
phrases.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَشۡرِي نَفۡسَهُ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ مَرۡضَاتِ ٱللَّهِۚ
phrases.explanation:
The word for selling was explained earlier, meaning that which is bought. And by seeking the good pleasure of Allah, the sense is that this seller, when he buys, seeks the good pleasure of Allah.

The interpreters differed concerning whom this verse is about. Some of them said that it was revealed concerning the emigrants and the helpers, and that those intended are the ones who fight in the path of Allah. Others said that it was revealed concerning certain men among the emigrants. And others said that what is intended is everyone who sells himself in obedience.

The view preferred is then given. It is what is related from Umar ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Abi Talib and from Ibn Abbas, that what is intended is the one who commands the right and forbids the wrong. And the report that the verse was revealed in the matter of Subayb is not objectionable.

The correct view is then given. Allah described one who sells himself seeking His good pleasure, so everyone who sells himself in obedience to Him until he is killed therein, or who seeks death even though he is not killed, is intended, whether that proceeded from him in the struggle against the enemy of the Muslims or in commanding the right.

phrases.translation: And Allah is Ever Gracious to ˹His˺ servants
phrases.ar: وَٱللَّهُ رَءُوفُۢ بِٱلۡعِبَادِ
phrases.explanation:
The explanation of the saying is then given. And Allah is gentle toward the servants, and the word for gentleness was demonstrated earlier, meaning the tenderness of mercy.

The meaning of it is then set out at length. Allah is possessor of a wide mercy toward His servant who sells himself for Him in the struggle against whoever turns against Him in His cause among the people of shirk and moral corruption, and toward the rest of His believing servants, in their near future and in their future place of return, so He fulfills for them the reward for what they have been tried with in obedience to Him in this world, and He causes them to dwell in His gardens for what they performed therein of that which is pleasing to Him.

phrases.translation: O believers! Enter into Islam wholeheartedly and do not follow Satan’s footsteps. Surely he is your sworn enemy
phrases.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱدۡخُلُواْ فِي ٱلسِّلۡمِ كَآفَّةٗ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ خُطُوَٰتِ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَكُمۡ عَدُوّٞ مُّبِينٞ
phrases.explanation:
The meaning of peace is discussed first. The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of the word for peace in this place. Some of them said that it means Islam, and others said that it means enter into obedience.

The recitation is then discussed. The reciters differed, most of the reciters of the people of Hijaz reciting it with the vowel that makes it peace, and most of the reciters of the people of Kufa with the other.

The question is then raised which of these two groups was called to enter all together into Islam. Some of them said that those called to it were the believers in Muhammad and in what he brought. Others said that those called to it were the believers in the prophets before him who denied Muhammad. And others said that the group called to peace, to whom it was said enter into it by this verse, are the people of the book, and they were commanded to enter into Islam.

The correct view is then given. Allah commanded those who believed to enter into acting according to all the legal ordinances of Islam, and under those who believed may fall those who believed in Muhammad and in what he brought and those who believed in the prophets and messengers before him, and He called both groups to act according to the legal ordinances and the prescribed punishments of Islam and to observe His obligations, and He forbade them to neglect anything of that, so the verse is general for everyone whom the name of faith encompasses.

The phrase all together is then explained, meaning collectively, all together.

The last clause is then explained. Act, O believers, according to all the legal ordinances of Islam, and enter into believing in it with word and deed, and leave the ways of Satan and his traces, lest you follow them, for verily he is for you an enemy whose enmity toward you is clear. And the way of Satan which He forbade them to follow is whatever contradicts the ruling and the legal ordinances of Islam, and to that belongs the keeping of the Sabbath and all other customs of the adherents of the religions that contradict the religion of Islam.

phrases.translation: If you falter after receiving the clear proofs, then know that Allah is indeed Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.ar: فَإِن زَلَلۡتُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَتۡكُمُ ٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتُ فَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
phrases.explanation: By this He means, but if you miss the truth, and thereby stray from it, and oppose Islam and its legal ordinances, after My proofs and the clear signs of My guidance have come to you, and the correctness of the matter of Islam has become clear to you through the indications that have cut off your excuse, then know that Allah is the Possessor of might, who is prevented by no obstacle from taking vengeance upon you and held back by no deterrer from punishing you for your opposition to His command, and All-Wise in what He does with you of punishment for your disobedience, after He has established the proof against you, and in all His other affairs.

phrases.translation: Are they waiting for Allah ˹Himself˺ to come to them in the shade of clouds, along with the angels?
phrases.ar: هَلۡ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَّآ أَن يَأۡتِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِي
phrases.explanation:
The question is explained first. Are those who declared the prophet and what he brought to be lies waiting for anything other than that Allah should come to them in shadows of clouds with the angels?

The recitation is then discussed. Some read the angels with the nominative, so that it is joined to the name of Allah, and others read it with the genitive, so that it is joined to the shadows.

The phrase are they waiting is then explained. It means they are not waiting, and that was expounded earlier.

Four views are then given. Some said that for that there is no further manner than that with which He has described Himself, the coming, the approaching and the descending, and it is not permitted for anyone to burden himself with a statement about that except on the basis of a report from Allah or from a sent messenger. Others said that His coming is like what is known of the coming of one who comes from one place to another. Others said that what is meant is that Allah's command should come to them, as one says that the Banu Umayya should come to us, by which their rule is meant. And others said that what is meant is that His reward, His reckoning and His punishment should come to them, as one says that the ruler cut off the thief, while in reality his helpers cut him off.

phrases.translation: ˹If He did˺, then the matter would be settled ˹at once˺. And to Allah ˹all˺ matters will be returned ˹for judgment˺
phrases.ar: ظُلَلٖ مِّنَ ٱلۡغَمَامِ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَقُضِيَ ٱلۡأَمۡرُۚ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُرۡجَعُ ٱلۡأُمُورُ
phrases.explanation:
A point of grammar is then given. Whoever read it as in shadows understood it as the plural of shadow, and the plural of that word takes two forms, just as the plural of friendship and of the covering takes two.

The exegetes differed over the words shadows of clouds, whether this is connected to the act of Allah or to the act of the angels. Some of them said that it is connected to the act of Allah, so the sense is that Allah should come to them in shadows of clouds and that the angels should come to them.

The statement of Ikrimah is then discussed, which agrees in part and differs in the manner of the angels, since it requires the genitive, he having interpreted the verse as Allah coming in shadows of clouds and in the angels.

The more correct interpretation is then given, that the words shadows of clouds are connected to the act of the Lord, so the sense is that Allah should come to them in shadows of clouds and that the angels should come to them. And the sense of the whole verse is given, that those who refrain from entering into the submission collectively and who follow the footsteps of Satan are waiting for anything other than that Allah should come to them in shadows of clouds, whereupon He decides in their case what He decides.

The closing clause is then explained at length. And to Allah all matters are returned means that to Allah returns the decision between His creatures on the day of resurrection, and the judgment between them in their affairs that occurred in the worldly life, of the wronging of one by another and the well-doing of the well-doer, so He separates between those who mutually wrong one another, requites the people of well-doing with bounty and the people of evil-doing with what He sees fit, and shows favour to whichever of them was not an unbeliever and forgives him. And He let His servants know that the return of all this is to Him at the standing place of the resurrection, so that He may do justice to everyone with respect to everyone, where there is no injustice and the weak and the strong are equal.

phrases.translation: Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs We have given them.
phrases.ar: سَلۡ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ كَمۡ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُم مِّنۡ ءَايَةِۭ بَيِّنَةٖۗ
phrases.explanation:
The command is explained first. Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs He has given them.

The sense of it is then set out. Ask, O Muhammad, those who expect nothing other than that He should come to them in shadows of clouds, and ask them how many a sign and proof He brought them before you with regard to what He imposed upon them of obligations. Yet they denied His proofs, gave the lie to His messengers, altered His favours toward them, and changed His covenant and His command to them.

phrases.translation: And whoever trades Allah’s favour—after receiving it—˹for disbelief˺ should know that Allah is indeed severe in punishment
phrases.ar: وَمَن يُبَدِّلۡ نِعۡمَةَ ٱللَّهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَتۡهُ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
phrases.explanation:
Allah informed His prophet of these signs only, and commanded him to be patient toward whoever gave him the lie and arrogantly exalted himself against his Lord, and He told him that the like of that was done by the predecessors of the communities before them toward their prophets, and that those among them who are from the Jews are remnants of those whose stories were related to him.

The second clause is then explained. And whoever changes the favor of Allah means whoever alters that which he promised Allah concerning His favor that is Islam, namely acting upon it and entering into it, and thus denies it, so He will punish him with the punishment He has held out in prospect for whoever denies it, and Allah is severe in His punishment.

The explanation of the verse is then given. O you who have believed in the Torah and have thus confirmed it, enter all of you into Islam and abandon disbelief and that to which Satan has called you of his error, for the clear proofs have come to you from Me by means of Muhammad. Therefore do not change My covenant to you. For whoever among you changes that, verily I will punish him with the painful punishment.

phrases.translation: The life of this world has been made appealing to the disbelievers, and they mock the believers. Those who are mindful ˹of Allah˺ will rank above them on the Day of Judgment.
phrases.ar: زُيِّنَ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَيَسۡخَرُونَ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْۘ وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوۡاْ فَوۡقَهُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۗ
phrases.explanation: The meaning is then given. For those who disbelieve, the love of the hastening worldly life with its pleasures has been made fair-seeming, so they strive therein to outdo one another in possessions and to boast over one another, and they seek positions of leadership and pomp, and they exalt themselves haughtily above following you, and they mock whoever follows you among the people of faith, because these people have abandoned the mutual outdoing in possessions and the boasting over the world by pursuing what is with Me. And those who have worked for Me and rejected the pleasures of the world are above those who disbelieve on the day of resurrection, in that the God-fearing are admitted into the garden and those who disbelieve into the fire.

phrases.translation: And Allah provides for whoever He wills without limit
phrases.ar: وَٱللَّهُ يَرۡزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ بِغَيۡرِ حِسَابٖ
phrases.explanation:
The clause is then explained. And Allah gives to those who are God-fearing on the day of resurrection of His favours, His honours and His abundant gifts, without reckoning them for the honour with which He has favoured them.

A question is then raised about what praise there is in the saying that He provides for whom He wills without reckoning. It is answered that the praise is the announcement that He does not fear the exhaustion of His storehouses, since reckoning occurs on the part of the giver only so that he may know the magnitude of the gift, so that he would not exceed what would cause him harm. But our Lord does not fear the exhaustion of His storehouses, nor any diminution of His possession through that which He gives, so that He would have need to reckon what He gives and to add up what remains.

phrases.translation: Humanity had once been one community ˹of believers before they lost faith˺. Then Allah raised prophets as deliverers of good news and as warners, and revealed to them the Scriptures in truth to judge among people regarding their disputes.
phrases.ar: كَانَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةٗ وَٰحِدَةٗ فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ وَأَنزَلَ مَعَهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ لِيَحۡكُمَ بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ فِيمَا ٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فِيهِۚ وَمَا ٱخۡتَلَفَ فِيهِ
phrases.explanation:
The scholars differed concerning the meaning of the community and of the people whom Allah described as having been one community. Some of them said that they are those who lived between Adam and Noah, and they were ten generations, all of them following a law of truth and then differing. Others said that Adam was upon the truth as a leader for his progeny, whereupon Allah sent the prophets among his descendants, and they directed the meaning of the community toward obedience to Allah, and the calling of the prophet of each generation was to those who had come to believe in the predecessor. And it is as though the one who proclaimed this view deemed it permissible to designate the individual by the name of the group, on account of the gathering of the good qualities in the one whom he called the community. Others said that the meaning is that mankind was one community upon one religion on the day He brought forth the progeny of Adam from his loins and showed them to Adam.

The correct interpretation is then given. Allah informed His servants that mankind was one community upon one religion and one creed, and He sent messengers who gave good tidings to whoever obeyed Allah of an abundant reward and a noble return, and who warned whoever disobeyed, and He sent down to them the Book in truth to judge between them concerning their disputes.

phrases.translation: And no one disputed the Scriptures except the very people who received them after clear proofs had come to them—out of jealousy.
phrases.ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوهُ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَتۡهُمُ ٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتُ بَغۡيَۢا بَيۡنَهُمۡۖ فَهَدَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ
phrases.explanation:
The clause is then explained. And none differed over it means none differed concerning the Book which He sent down, namely the Torah, except those who were given it, by which He means the Jews of the Children of Israel, and the reason for their differing was out of mutual transgression, which is derived from the saying of a person that he transgressed against another when he tyrannized over him and overstepped his bounds.

A point of grammar is then added, and the question is raised about the particle in after the clear proofs had come to them.

Two views are then given. On the first, the particle belongs to those who were given the Book and what follows it is a subordinate clause to it. On the second, the particle belongs to the coming of the proofs, so the sense is that the people differed after the proofs came to them and out of mutual transgression.

The second view is then preferred, for the people differed only after the proof had been established against them and the clear proofs of Allah had come, and likewise they differed only out of mutual transgression.

phrases.translation: Then Allah, by His grace, has guided the believers to the truth regarding those disputes. And Allah guides whoever He wills to the Straight Path
phrases.ar: ءَامَنُواْ لِمَا ٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ بِإِذۡنِهِۦۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٖ مُّسۡتَقِيمٍ
phrases.explanation:
Then Allah guided means that Allah granted right discernment to those who believed, and they are the people of faith in Allah and in His messenger, who believed him and believed in that with which he came, to the truth concerning which these factions among the Children of Israel differed, by His proof and His Book.

And the phrase by His permission is explained as through His knowledge of that to which He guided them. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path means that He grants right direction to whom He wills of His creation and directs him to the straight way upon the truth in which there is no crookedness. And in this verse lies the clear exposition of the correctness of what the people of truth said, that every favor to the servants, in their religion or their worldly life, is from Allah.

A question is then raised whether He guided them to the truth or to the disagreement, and it is answered that the meaning is only that He guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which those who were given the Book differed, so that some of them accept it and others deny it.

phrases.translation: Do you think you will be admitted into Paradise without being tested like those before you? They were afflicted with suffering and adversity and were so ˹violently˺ shaken that ˹even˺ the Messenger and the believers with him cried out, “When will Allah’s help come?” Indeed, Allah’s help is ˹always˺ near
phrases.ar: أَمۡ حَسِبۡتُمۡ أَن تَدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَلَمَّا يَأۡتِكُم مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوۡاْ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۖ مَّسَّتۡهُمُ ٱلۡبَأۡسَآءُ وَٱلضَّرَّآءُ وَزُلۡزِلُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَ ٱلرَّسُولُ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُۥ مَتَىٰ نَصۡرُ ٱللَّهِۗ أَلَآ إِنَّ نَصۡرَ ٱللَّهِ قَرِيبٞ
phrases.explanation:
The question is explained first. Or did you suppose is as though He poses a question at the outset without an interrogative particle preceding it.

The meaning of the statement is then given. Or did you suppose, O you who believe in Allah and His messengers, that you would enter Paradise without there having befallen you the like of what befell those who were before you, namely the followers of the messengers who were tested before you with the like of what you are tested with, so that you might be like them.

The occasion is then given. This verse was revealed on the Day of the Trench, when the believers underwent what they underwent of severe hardship through the fear of the Confederates, and the report naming those who said that is given.

The phrase is then explained, meaning the like of those who passed away and thus went by before you, and the word for likeness was shown elsewhere to mean likeness and semblance. And the shaking is explained as merely the fear of the enemy and not the earthquake, and for that reason it was of long duration.

phrases.translation: They ask you ˹O Prophet in˺ what ˹way˺ they should donate.
phrases.explanation: People ask how they should give in charity, and the answer directs attention to recipients. The question reflects concern about practical generosity. The verse turns worship into care for family and vulnerable people, emphasizing that giving should respond to real needs.  The answer makes charity responsive to relationships and urgent need.

phrases.translation: Say, “Whatever donations you give are for parents, relatives, orphans, the poor, and ˹needy˺ travellers.
phrases.explanation: Charity should benefit parents, relatives, orphans, the poor, and travelers in need. The order highlights family obligations alongside wider social care. Whatever good is given is known to God, so sincere generosity matters even when the amount or recipient is not publicly recognized.  This list encourages generosity within both family and the broader community.

phrases.translation: Whatever good you do is certainly well known to Allah.”
phrases.explanation: God knows every good act and its intention, whether or not people witness it. This assurance encourages sincere giving without seeking praise. It also reminds donors that charity is evaluated by God, so generosity should be joined with honesty, care, and respect for those receiving support.

phrases.translation: Fighting has been made obligatory upon you ˹believers˺, though you dislike it.
phrases.explanation: The verse addresses a prescribed duty to fight in a particular context, acknowledging that believers may naturally dislike armed conflict. This is not a general endorsement of violence, but a difficult obligation governed by surrounding limits and circumstances. The acknowledgment of reluctance recognizes the human cost of conflict.

phrases.translation: Perhaps you dislike something which is good for you and like something which is bad for you.
phrases.explanation: Human preferences do not always align with what is ultimately beneficial or harmful. Believers may dislike a duty that serves justice or protection, and desire something damaging. The verse calls for humility about limited knowledge and trust in God’s wisdom.  Human judgment is partial, especially when future outcomes remain unseen.

phrases.translation: Allah knows and you do not know
phrases.explanation: God’s knowledge encompasses outcomes people cannot foresee. This reminder helps believers approach difficult commands with humility rather than assuming their immediate feelings reveal the full truth. It does not remove the need for ethical limits, but grounds trust in God’s superior knowledge.  The reminder supports humility, not reckless action or cruelty.

phrases.translation: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about fighting in the sacred months.
phrases.explanation: People question fighting during months traditionally regarded as sacred. The verse answers within the context of ongoing hostilities and persecution. It does not erase the sanctity of these months, but compares the act with other violations and harms occurring at the time.  The question arises from a specific period of conflict and sacred observance.

phrases.translation: Say, “Fighting during these months is a great sin.
phrases.explanation: Fighting in a sacred month is acknowledged as a grave matter. The verse does not dismiss the prohibition or treat it lightly. It then explains that other acts, including persecution and expulsion, can be even more serious in the circumstances under discussion.  The response acknowledges the seriousness of violating sacred time.

phrases.translation: But hindering ˹others˺ from the Path of Allah, rejecting Him, and expelling the worshippers from the Sacred Mosque is ˹a˺ greater ˹sin˺ in the sight of Allah.
phrases.explanation: Preventing people from worship, rejecting God, and expelling believers from the Sacred Mosque are described as greater wrongs in this setting. The verse responds to accusations by recognizing the wider pattern of persecution. It places events in context rather than isolating one incident from prior aggression.

phrases.translation: For persecution is far worse than killing.
phrases.explanation: Persecution that suppresses faith and drives people from worship is presented as worse than killing. The statement emphasizes the grave harm of systematic oppression. It provides context for the conflict passages while not authorizing indiscriminate violence or removing the limits set elsewhere.  This comparison concerns oppression and coercion described in the passage.

phrases.translation: And they will not stop fighting you until they turn you away from your faith—if they can.
phrases.explanation: The verse warns that hostile opponents may continue fighting until believers abandon their faith. It describes the danger of coercion and religious persecution. The warning encourages vigilance and steadfastness, not hatred toward all people of another faith.  The warning is tied to hostile conduct, not identity alone.

phrases.translation: And whoever among you renounces their own faith and dies a disbeliever, their deeds will become void in this life and in the Hereafter.
phrases.explanation: The verse warns of the spiritual consequence for someone who abandons faith and dies in disbelief. It emphasizes the seriousness of a final rejection, not a temporary struggle or a person who later repents. The outcome concerns ultimate accountability before God.  The condition of dying in disbelief is central to this warning.

phrases.translation: It is they who will be the residents of the Fire.
phrases.explanation: Those who persist in disbelief until death face punishment in the Fire. This statement follows the condition in the preceding clause and should not be used to make careless judgments about individuals. It is a serious warning about the consequence of a final rejection.  The warning concerns those who persist in rejection to the end.

phrases.translation: They will be there forever.”
phrases.explanation: The verse describes the punishment as lasting for those specified. The severity underscores the importance of faith and repentance during life, when turning back remains possible. The passage balances warning with the next verse’s assurance of mercy for believers who strive sincerely.  This consequence should prompt reflection during life, not despair.

phrases.translation: Surely those who have believed, emigrated, and struggled in the Way of Allah—they can hope for Allah’s mercy.
phrases.explanation: Believers who emigrated and struggled in God’s cause are encouraged to hope for divine mercy. Their sacrifice reflects commitment under difficult circumstances, but the verse directs hope to God rather than self-congratulation. Mercy remains the ultimate gift, and sincere effort is met with compassion.  Their migration and struggle were responses to difficult circumstances.

phrases.translation: And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: God’s forgiveness and mercy provide the basis for hope. The attributes reassure those who have endured and remind everyone that salvation is not earned through effort alone. The verse ends the discussion of faith and struggle with confidence in divine compassion.  Forgiveness and mercy are offered by God, not claimed as entitlement.

phrases.translation: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about intoxicants and gambling.
phrases.explanation: People ask about intoxicants and gambling, practices that can affect judgment, family life, and social wellbeing. The answer weighs their harms and benefits rather than treating the question as trivial. It guides believers toward reflection and responsible conduct.  The question invites a reasoned moral assessment of their effects.

phrases.translation: Say, “There is great evil in both, as well as some benefit for people—but the evil outweighs the benefit.”
phrases.explanation: Intoxicants and gambling may bring some perceived benefit, but their harms outweigh those advantages. The verse directs attention to the broader consequences rather than isolated gains. It provides moral reasoning that prepares people to avoid practices that damage judgment, wealth, and relationships.  The comparison weighs long-term damage against short-term pleasure.

phrases.translation: They ˹also˺ ask you ˹O Prophet˺ what they should donate.
phrases.explanation: A second question concerns what amount of wealth to give. The verse answers in a way that encourages generosity without requiring people to give beyond their capacity. It shifts the focus from calculation toward thoughtful care for others.  The guidance promotes giving within one’s genuine capacity.

phrases.translation: Say, “Whatever you can spare.”
phrases.explanation: People should give from what they can afford beyond essential needs. The instruction makes charity practical and sustainable, while encouraging generosity. It does not require impoverishing oneself, and it leaves room for people to consider dependents and responsibilities.  Sustainable giving allows care for dependents alongside generosity.

phrases.translation: This is how Allah makes His revelations clear to you ˹believers˺, so perhaps you may reflect
phrases.explanation: God clarifies these matters so believers can consider their implications. Reflection helps people recognize harmful practices and make wise choices about wealth. The verse invites thoughtful application of revelation in everyday life rather than unthinking compliance.  Reflection enables believers to apply guidance with understanding. The advice includes both material and moral dimensions.

phrases.translation: upon this world and the Hereafter.
phrases.explanation: Believers are encouraged to reflect on both worldly life and the hereafter. This perspective helps them weigh immediate benefits against lasting consequences. The verse links moral decisions with a broader view of human responsibility and final accountability.  A balanced perspective prevents immediate needs from becoming ultimate goals.

phrases.translation: And they ask you ˹O Prophet˺ concerning orphans.
phrases.explanation: The community asks how to deal with orphans and their property. Their vulnerability makes careful treatment especially important. The answer emphasizes improvement and responsible partnership, guiding people away from neglect or exploitation.  The question concerns the ethical treatment of especially vulnerable children. The aim is their welfare, not merely administrative convenience.

phrases.translation: Say, “Improving their condition is best.
phrases.explanation: The best approach is to improve orphans’ welfare and manage their affairs in their interest. This principle requires care, fairness, and attention to their needs. It makes protection and benefit the standard for decisions involving those who depend on adults.  Improving their condition is the guiding aim of guardianship.

phrases.translation: And if you partner with them, they are bonded with you ˹in faith˺.
phrases.explanation: If guardians combine their affairs with those of orphans, they should remember that the children are fellow believers and members of the household. The phrase permits practical partnership while requiring trust and fairness. It rejects isolating orphans when shared arrangements can benefit them.  Shared household arrangements remain subject to fair treatment.

phrases.translation: And Allah knows who intends harm and who intends good.
phrases.explanation: God knows the intentions behind a guardian’s actions, including whether arrangements truly benefit the orphan. This assurance comforts those acting sincerely and warns exploiters that concealment will not hide wrongdoing. Intention and conduct both matter in managing another person’s property.  Divine knowledge safeguards those whose interests may be hidden.

phrases.translation: Had Allah willed, He could have made it difficult for you.
phrases.explanation: God could have imposed a much stricter separation, but He has allowed practical arrangements that benefit orphans. The verse recognizes human circumstances while preserving the requirement of good intent. Ease is not permission to exploit, but an allowance to manage affairs responsibly.  The allowance must be used for benefit, not self-interest.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.”
phrases.explanation: God’s power and wisdom govern these rulings. His wisdom balances protection of vulnerable people with practical arrangements for their care. The attributes close the guidance with a reminder that believers should trust the rule and act with integrity.  Wisdom and might support the fairness of the instruction.

phrases.translation: Do not marry polytheistic women until they believe;
phrases.explanation: The verse instructs believers not to enter marriage with polytheists until they believe in God. It prioritizes shared faith over social attraction or status. The command is part of its specific religious and historical framework, and concerns marriage commitments rather than permission to mistreat anyone.

phrases.translation: for a believing slave-woman is better than a free polytheist, even though she may look pleasant to you.
phrases.explanation: The comparison challenges status-based preferences: a believing woman, even enslaved in the historical setting, is presented as preferable to a free polytheist whom one finds attractive. It emphasizes faith over social rank and appearance. The verse does not endorse slavery, but addresses people within a society where it existed.

phrases.translation: And do not marry your women to polytheistic men until they believe,
phrases.explanation: The same concern is applied to women’s marriage choices: believers are told not to marry them to polytheist men until they believe. The instruction underscores the importance of shared faith in marriage and does not frame women as property. It establishes a religious boundary for the community.

phrases.translation: for a believing slave-man is better than a free polytheist, even though he may look pleasant to you.
phrases.explanation: A believing man, even one enslaved in that society, is described as preferable to a free polytheist who is socially or physically appealing. The comparison reverses assumptions about status and attractiveness. Its emphasis is faith, while the historical reference should not be read as approval of enslavement.

phrases.translation: They invite ˹you˺ to the Fire while Allah invites ˹you˺ to Paradise and forgiveness by His grace.
phrases.explanation: The verse contrasts influences that lead away from God with God’s invitation to Paradise and forgiveness. Marriage is treated as a serious bond that can shape spiritual life, not merely social standing. The invitation is by divine grace, reminding believers that salvation is a gift.

phrases.translation: He makes His revelations clear to the people so perhaps they will be mindful
phrases.explanation: God clarifies these instructions so people may understand and act with mindfulness. The aim is not arbitrary restriction but thoughtful obedience and awareness of consequences. The verse closes by calling the community to reflect on the guidance before making important choices.  Clarity supports informed choices and responsible religious conduct.

phrases.translation: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about menstruation.
phrases.explanation: The community asks about menstruation and marital conduct. The question receives practical guidance that respects bodily conditions and clarifies boundaries. This is a matter of health and worship practice, and the answer addresses intercourse during the menstrual period specifically.  The response concerns a recurring bodily condition and practical marital guidance.

phrases.translation: Say, “Beware of its harm!
phrases.explanation: The response identifies menstruation as a time involving harm or discomfort. The guidance asks spouses to take this condition seriously and avoid causing injury. It does not imply that menstruating women are impure as people or should be socially excluded.  The concern is avoiding physical harm, not stigmatizing the person menstruating.

phrases.translation: So keep away, and do not have intercourse with your wives during their monthly cycles until they are purified.
phrases.explanation: The restriction is specifically on sexual intercourse during menstruation until the period has ended and purification occurs. It is not a command to avoid all affection or companionship. The verse sets a clear boundary while respecting the physical wellbeing of spouses.  The restriction is limited to intercourse during the specified period.

phrases.translation: When they purify themselves, then you may approach them in the manner specified by Allah.
phrases.explanation: After the menstrual period and purification, marital intercourse is permitted within God’s limits. The wording preserves both the boundary and the return to ordinary intimacy. The instruction should be understood with mutual respect and care, not as coercion.  The permission resumes only after the stated purification.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah loves those who always turn to Him in repentance and those who purify themselves.”
phrases.explanation: God loves those who repent and those who purify themselves. The conclusion links spiritual return with physical cleanliness while distinguishing the two concepts. It encourages sincere self-correction and respectful observance of purification practices.  Repentance and cleanliness both involve returning to a sound state.  The paired qualities support a balanced view of bodily and spiritual wellbeing.

phrases.translation: Your wives are like farmland for you,
phrases.explanation: The agricultural metaphor refers to procreation within marriage and should not reduce wives to property or deny their personhood. The surrounding guidance and the translation’s explicit reference to consent call for mutual respect. The image concerns marital intimacy and its potential for family life.  The metaphor must be read alongside mutual dignity and the explicit consent language.

phrases.translation: so approach them ˹consensually˺ as you please.
phrases.explanation: Spouses may approach one another within the limits God has set, and the translation emphasizes consent. The verse does not authorize coercion or harm. It gives flexibility within marriage while maintaining ethical and religious boundaries.  Both partners retain their rights and responsibilities within marriage.  Respectful intimacy is compatible with religious limits.

phrases.translation: And send forth something good for yourselves.
phrases.explanation: The phrase encourages spouses to invest in good for their future, including righteous conduct and care for family. Intimacy is placed within a broader moral life rather than treated as an isolated pleasure. The wording invites preparation for the hereafter through responsible choices.  Good conduct and care extend beyond the intimate relationship.

phrases.translation: Be mindful of Allah, and know that you will meet Him.
phrases.explanation: Spouses are reminded that God-consciousness applies within private family life as well as public worship. They will meet God and answer for their conduct. The reminder underscores dignity, consent, and moral responsibility in intimate relationships.  Privacy does not exempt spouses from ethical accountability.  Accountability remains present even in private family life.

phrases.translation: And give good news to the believers
phrases.explanation: Believers who heed this guidance are offered good news. The phrase closes with reassurance after practical instructions about marriage. It encourages the community to follow divine limits with faith and confidence in God’s reward.  The message offers encouragement to those who observe the guidance.  This close applies to all believers who act faithfully.

phrases.translation: Do not use Allah’s Name in your oaths as an excuse for not doing good,
phrases.explanation: People should not swear by God as a pretext for refusing to do good. An oath must not become a barrier to generosity or reconciliation. The verse discourages turning religious language into a shield for inaction.  Vows should not obstruct generosity toward people in need.

phrases.translation: not guarding against evil,
phrases.explanation: Oaths should not prevent people from avoiding wrongdoing or pursuing what is morally right. God’s name must not be invoked to justify neglect of ethical responsibility. The phrase broadens the warning from charity to general conduct.  Moral responsibility is more important than preserving a harmful excuse.

phrases.translation: or not making peace between people.
phrases.explanation: Believers should not use an oath to avoid reconciling people or repairing relationships. Peacemaking is a valued good, and a prior vow should not become an excuse to abandon it. The verse promotes practical efforts to reduce conflict.  Reconciliation can restore trust and prevent lasting division.

phrases.translation: And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: God hears the oaths people make and knows their intentions. This awareness prevents people from hiding behind technical wording while neglecting good. The attributes encourage sincerity and accountability in the use of vows and religious speech.  Sincere intentions matter alongside the words people choose.  The reminder encourages sincerity in public and private speech.

phrases.translation: Allah will not hold you accountable for unintentional oaths,
phrases.explanation: God does not hold people accountable for casual or unintended oaths that are not deliberate commitments. This distinction prevents excessive burden over words spoken without serious intent. The verse treats intention as relevant to moral responsibility.  This rule prevents casual expressions from becoming unintended burdens.

phrases.translation: but for what you intended in your hearts.
phrases.explanation: Accountability concerns what people deliberately intend. Inner purpose matters alongside spoken words, so an oath made knowingly cannot be dismissed as accidental. The phrase directs believers to sincerity and care in making commitments.  The heart’s purpose distinguishes a deliberate vow from careless speech.  Deliberate intention is what gives a serious oath its moral weight.

phrases.translation: And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Forbearing
phrases.explanation: God forgives and is forbearing toward people, giving them room to correct their conduct. These attributes temper the discussion of accountability and reassure those who repent. The verse encourages responsible speech without despair over human mistakes.  Forbearance allows people time to correct mistakes and seek forgiveness.

phrases.translation: Those who swear not to have intercourse with their wives must wait for four months.
phrases.explanation: The verse gives a time limit for a husband’s oath of sexual abstention from his wife. The waiting period prevents indefinite suspension of the marriage and protects the wife from being left without resolution. It regulates a serious domestic dispute with a defined boundary.  The fixed period protects the wife from prolonged uncertainty.

phrases.translation: If they change their mind, then Allah is certainly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: If the husband returns to marital relations, God’s forgiveness and mercy are affirmed. The verse offers a path to reconciliation rather than insisting that an oath must prolong harm. It encourages resolving the dispute with compassion and taking responsibility for one’s words.  Reconciliation should be accompanied by sincere care and restored rights.

phrases.translation: But if they settle on divorce,
phrases.explanation: If the spouses do not reconcile and the husband decides on divorce, the matter proceeds to separation. The transition distinguishes returning to the marriage from choosing its end. The surrounding family-law verses regulate these decisions to protect rights and prevent indefinite uncertainty.  The option to separate must be handled through the established protections.

phrases.translation: then Allah is indeed All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: God hears what is said in the process and knows the intentions behind it. Divorce is not outside divine accountability. These attributes encourage honesty, fairness, and care for the rights of both spouses.  Divine awareness reinforces the obligation to act justly during separation.  The matter remains known to God even when hidden from others.

phrases.translation: Divorced women must wait three monthly cycles ˹before they can re-marry˺.
phrases.explanation: A waiting period of three cycles is prescribed before a divorced woman remarries. It clarifies the transition after divorce and may establish whether she is pregnant. The rule structures the period of separation and should be applied with respect for women’s rights and circumstances.  The waiting period also protects clarity about lineage and responsibilities.

phrases.translation: It is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs,
phrases.explanation: Women are not to conceal a pregnancy or other relevant condition during the waiting period. Honest disclosure protects the rights and responsibilities of all involved, especially the child. The phrase places a duty of truthfulness within the legal process.  Concealment could affect rights, obligations, and the welfare of a child.

phrases.translation: if they ˹truly˺ believe in Allah and the Last Day.
phrases.explanation: Faith and accountability before the Last Day ground the obligation to be truthful. The phrase stresses that religious commitment should shape private legal conduct as well as public worship. God knows what is hidden, so honesty is ultimately accountable to Him.  Belief should motivate honesty even when disclosure is personally difficult.

phrases.translation: And their husbands reserve the right to take them back within that period if they desire reconciliation.
phrases.explanation: During the waiting period, a husband may restore the marriage with the intention of reconciliation. The stated purpose is repair, not using revocation to harm or control the woman. The provision exists within regulated divorce procedures and calls for sincere efforts to reconcile.  Reconciliation must be genuine and not a device for causing harm.

phrases.translation: Women have rights similar to those of men equitably,
phrases.explanation: Women are affirmed to have rights comparable to their responsibilities, according to fairness. The phrase establishes reciprocity and dignity within marriage. It should be read as a principle of equitable treatment, alongside the specific rights and duties described in family law.  Rights and duties are presented as reciprocal rather than one-sided.

phrases.translation: although men have a degree ˹of responsibility˺ above them.
phrases.explanation: The verse acknowledges a degree of responsibility assigned to men in this legal and historical context. It does not erase women’s rights or justify abuse. The surrounding statement of equitable rights requires any responsibility to be exercised with justice and accountability.  Responsibility does not nullify equitable treatment or human dignity.

phrases.translation: And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: God’s might and wisdom frame the legal guidance. His authority does not negate the need for humans to apply the rules fairly. The attributes remind spouses and communities that family decisions remain accountable to divine justice.  The reminder discourages misuse of authority in family matters.

phrases.translation: Divorce may be retracted twice,
phrases.explanation: The verse limits revocable divorce to two occasions, preventing repeated threats from keeping a wife in uncertainty. The limit protects the stability and dignity of marriage. After these chances, the husband must choose either honorable retention or a gracious separation.  Limiting revocation prevents spouses being kept in repeated limbo.

phrases.translation: then the husband must retain ˹his wife˺ with honour or separate ˹from her˺ with grace.
phrases.explanation: After a revocable divorce, the husband must either continue the marriage honorably or end it without cruelty. The verse rejects using reconciliation to inflict harm. Fairness and dignity govern both outcomes.  The choice must protect dignity whichever path is taken.  Separation should be gracious and free from degrading treatment.

phrases.translation: It is not lawful for husbands to take back anything of the dowry given to their wives,
phrases.explanation: A husband may not reclaim the dowry as a condition of ending the marriage. The rule protects a wife’s financial right and prevents coercive extraction. It establishes that divorce does not permit a husband to seize what has been given to her.  The dowry belongs to the wife and is not a bargaining weapon.

phrases.translation: unless the couple fears not being able to keep within the limits of Allah.
phrases.explanation: An exception is recognized when the spouses fear they cannot maintain the limits and responsibilities of marriage. This acknowledges that a marriage may become untenable despite efforts. The next clause provides a process for a wife to seek release by compensation.  The exception is grounded in genuine inability to fulfill obligations.

phrases.translation: So if you fear they will not be able to keep within the limits of Allah, there is no blame if the wife compensates the husband to obtain divorce.
phrases.explanation: If the couple cannot maintain the marriage’s obligations, the wife may offer compensation to obtain divorce. This provision allows her a route out of a harmful or unworkable marriage. It should not be used to pressure a wife into surrendering rights unjustly.  The process should be voluntary and free from coercion.

phrases.translation: These are the limits set by Allah, so do not transgress them.
phrases.explanation: The rules are divine limits that must not be violated. The warning applies to both spouses and anyone administering the process. Respecting boundaries protects people from coercion, retaliation, and exploitation during divorce.  The limit guards against abuse of legal permissions.  Both partners and community authorities must respect these boundaries.

phrases.translation: And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah, they are the ˹true˺ wrongdoers
phrases.explanation: Those who violate these limits commit wrongdoing. The statement reinforces that legal procedure must be governed by justice, not personal power. It calls all parties to honor the rights and protections established in the passage.  Individual power cannot override justice and established rights.  The warning includes anyone who knowingly abuses the procedure.

phrases.translation: So if a husband divorces his wife ˹three times˺,
phrases.explanation: The verse addresses a final divorce after the earlier opportunities for revocation. It sets a boundary against treating divorce as a repeated threat without consequence. The rule is part of a structured family-law framework and should not be confused with casual or impulsive declarations.  The rule makes the finality of this divorce unmistakable.

phrases.translation: then it is not lawful for him to remarry her until after she has married another man and then is divorced.
phrases.explanation: After a final divorce, the former spouses cannot simply remarry one another immediately. The verse describes a subsequent genuine marriage that later ends, not a contrived arrangement. The rule underscores the seriousness and finality of the prior divorce.  The condition cannot be staged merely to bypass the rule.

phrases.translation: Then it is permissible for them to reunite, as long as they feel they are able to maintain the limits of Allah.
phrases.explanation: If the later marriage ends and the former spouses wish to reunite, they may do so if they believe they can uphold God’s limits. Reconciliation is not automatic, it requires mutual willingness and a realistic commitment to fairness and responsibility.  Reconciliation requires a serious intention to observe mutual rights.

phrases.translation: These are the limits set by Allah, which He makes clear for people of knowledge
phrases.explanation: God makes these family-law limits clear so people can understand and observe them. Knowledge helps prevent manipulation and protect rights. The verse concludes by emphasizing clarity, learning, and accountability in decisions with serious consequences for families.  Clear knowledge helps prevent manipulation and protect families.  People should consult the guidance rather than act on assumptions.

phrases.translation: When you divorce women and they have ˹almost˺ reached the end of their waiting period, either retain them honourably or let them go honourably.
phrases.explanation: As the waiting period nears its end, a husband must either reconcile honorably or allow the divorce to conclude honorably. The choice should be made with respect for the woman’s dignity and rights. The verse rejects using the waiting period to keep someone in uncertainty or exert power.

phrases.translation: But do not retain them ˹only˺ to harm them ˹or˺ to take advantage ˹of them˺.
phrases.explanation: A husband must not revoke a divorce merely to harm his wife or prolong control over her.
